target.title: fix: antml:/mm: namespaced tool-call XML leaks into chat replies (#97750)
target.body:
Closes #97750

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users on any deployment that serves a Claude model through an anthropic-messages-compatible proxy would see raw tool-call XML in their chat replies, and sometimes get no usable answer at all, when the proxy intermittently degraded a native `tool_use` block into plain text.

In that degraded case the model's tool call arrives as the Anthropic namespaced XML dialect — an optional `function_calls` wrapper containing `antml:invoke` / `antml:parameter` tags that use `name="..."` attributes (MiniMax emits the same shape with an `mm:` prefix). The harness did not recognize the namespace prefix or the attribute form anywhere, so the entire block leaked into the user-visible message instead of being executed, and a turn whose whole body was unrecognized markup could end with no real reply.

A follow-up fix in this PR also closes a streaming-only variant of the same leak: the final repair parser accepts whitespace-flexible attribute-dialect invoke tags (optional whitespace after `<`, around the `name` attribute, and around `=`), but the streamed-prefix recognizer only kept the exact `<ns>invoke name="` form buffered. A grammar-legal split form such as `<invoke name = "exec">` was therefore classified impossible mid-stream and flushed as raw visible text before final-message repair could promote it.

## Why This Change Was Made

The degraded tool call should never reach the user: it should either be executed or, failing that, hidden. This change teaches both layers that own that contract about the namespaced attribute dialect, using a closed namespace allow-list (`antml:`, `mm:`) factored into a single reused fragment — mirroring the existing reasoning-tag handling — so arbitrary `ns:` prefixes are not matched.

- Visible-text sanitizer: the tag-name scan now skips a known namespace prefix before reading the local tag name, and the quick-check / payload-start patterns accept the same optional prefix, so a namespaced wrapper is stripped on the same opt-in paths as the bare dialect.
- Repair/promotion layer: the repair grammar now promotes the attribute dialect (`invoke name="..."` / `parameter name="..."`, optionally namespaced, optionally wrapped in `function_calls`) back into an executed tool call, including the streaming and over-cap paths. Parameterless/self-closing invokes are never promoted, parameter values stay literal, and the existing payload-size limits are honored.
- Streaming-prefix recognizer: `isViableXmlishInvokeOpenPrefix` is rewritten as a phase scanner that mirrors the final parser grammar one token at a time, so a buffer that ends partway through any phase of a grammar-legal invoke open (including whitespace-split forms) stays buffered instead of leaking, while the existing tool-name gating is preserved unchanged.
- `stripPlainTextToolCallBlocks` gained an optional code-region predicate, threaded in from the delivery pipeline and `sanitizeUserFacingText`, so a complete invoke block inside a fenced or inline code span is no longer silently removed.

Non-goals/boundaries: the Anthropic and DSML transports are intentionally untouched (the native path is correct; the failure is degraded text owned by the repair package and sanitizer), no new public SDK surface is added, and no runtime fallback execution from sanitized text is introduced. The equals dialect (`<function=...>`/`<parameter=...>`), bracket, and Harmony paths are unchanged.

## User Impact

Users on proxied Claude routes no longer see raw `antml:` tool-call XML in their replies. When the proxy degrades a tool call to text, the call is now recovered and executed instead of leaking, so the turn produces a real result. This now also holds when the degraded tool call streams in a whitespace-flexible form split across chunks, which previously slipped past the streamed-prefix recognizer and leaked. Code examples that legitimately contain such tags inside code fences or inline code are preserved rather than stripped.

## Evidence

Focused unit tests cover both layers and the edge cases:

- Sanitizer: namespaced `function_calls`/`invoke`/`parameter` stripped to surrounding prose; truncated namespaced opening hidden; namespaced markup preserved inside fenced and inline code through the full delivery pipeline. Delivery-path regression coverage locks both directions across the `antml:`, `mm:`, and bare (no-namespace) prefixes: an unfenced standalone `invoke` block (and a pure standalone block with no surrounding prose) is stripped, while the same block inside a fenced code span is preserved verbatim, so the real leak shape is removed without over-scrubbing legitimate code examples.
- Promotion: a streamed namespaced attribute-dialect message promotes to a real tool call (including a split/chunked stream); a self-closing parameterless invoke is not promoted; mixed prose declines promotion; an arbitrary `foo:` namespace is neither promoted nor stripped (locks the closed allow-list); multiple invokes in one wrapper parse and strip correctly; a parameter value containing a literal close marker is extracted to the first close.
- Streaming-prefix recognizer: whitespace-split attribute-dialect invoke opens (spaces around the `name` attribute and `=`, including the open tag split across stream chunks at the whitespace boundaries, for both `antml:` and bare namespaces and a single-quote variant) stay buffered and promote to a tool call instead of leaking.
- Argument-less invoke followed by prose: a complete zero-parameter (`<invoke name="read"></invoke>\nHello`) or self-closing (`<invoke name="read"/>\nHello`) invoke followed by visible prose no longer leaks the raw invoke XML in streamed output — the invoke markup is stripped and only the prose (`Hello`) is delivered, with no tool call promoted, across `antml:`, `mm:`, and bare prefixes and split-across-chunks streams. Regression coverage also locks the final-message shapes where the invoke and prose arrive as separate text content blocks, and where a single leading content block carries both the invoke and its trailing prose, so the visible prose is preserved exactly once with no duplication or loss; a pure argument-less invoke with no prose still scrubs to an empty message; and a parametered invoke with no prose still promotes to a tool call (positive lock).

Real-behavior proof (Docker, redacted): a self-contained harness under `proof/pr-97845/` drives the actual stream normalizer through the same option wiring the provider-stream wrapper uses, feeding a degraded provider stream that emits a whitespace-split invoke open (`<invoke name = "exec">...`) split across chunks at the whitespace boundaries. Captured runtime output shows the regression and its fix:

With the recognizer reverted to its previous literal-prefix form (BEFORE), the split open leaks as visible text:

```
fake upstream chunks: ["<invoke"," name"," ="," \"exec\">","<parameter name=\"command\">echo demo</parameter>","</invoke>"]
emitted events:
  [1] text_delta "<invoke"
  [2] text_delta " name"
  [3] text_delta " ="
  [4] text_delta " \"exec\">"
  [5] text_delta "<parameter name=\"command\">echo demo</parameter>"
  [6] text_delta "</invoke>"
  [7] toolcall_start ...
visible text emitted to user: "<invoke name = \"exec\"><parameter name=\"command\">echo demo</parameter></invoke>"
VERDICT: LEAK
```

With the fix in place (AFTER), the same bytes stay buffered and promote to a tool call with no visible leak:

```
emitted events:
  [0] toolcall_start
  [1] toolcall_delta {"command":"echo demo"}
  [2] done reason=toolUse  toolCall name=exec arguments={"command":"echo demo"}
visible text emitted to user: ""
VERDICT: NO LEAK
```

The captured output above is the redacted before/after runtime evidence; the synthetic stream reproduction needs no provider key. (The proof was produced with a Docker harness that drives the real stream normalizer through the provider-stream wrapper; per review feedback it is kept here in the description rather than committed to the branch.)

Local validation:

```
node scripts/test-projects.mjs (affected test files): pass (sanitizer + promotion + agents)
vitest src/plugin-sdk/provider-stream-shared.test.ts: 92 pass (incl. new whitespace-split and argument-less-invoke-plus-prose regressions)
pnpm tsgo:core && pnpm tsgo:core:test: clean
oxlint on changed source files: 0 warnings, 0 errors
oxfmt --check on changed files: all correctly formatted
```

target.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context
target.body:
## Summary

Fix event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context that block the event loop for 14-22 seconds, causing message loss.

### Root causes addressed

1. **Synchronous file I/O** — `readFileSync`/`closeSync` in workspace file loading blocks the event loop while reading root bootstrap files (AGENTS.md, SOUL.md, etc.)
2. **Unbounded blocking glob walks** — `fs.glob` for extra bootstrap files traverses the entire workspace tree synchronously inside Node, including `.git`/`node_modules` directories, without yielding to the event loop
3. **Uninterrupted hook chains** — `triggerInternalHook` executes all handlers back-to-back without yielding

### Changes

**`src/agents/workspace.ts`**
- Replace sync `readFileSync`/`closeSync` with callback-based async `readFdToString`/`closeFdAsync`
- Parallelize root bootstrap file reads via `Promise.all` (previously serial `for` loop)
- Replace `fs.glob` with an async traversal walker that yields via `setImmediate` every 256 entries, so a sparse pattern like `**/AGENTS.md` over a large workspace never blocks the event loop. The walker performs no directory pruning — it walks the full tree and returns every file matching the configured patterns, with no traversal cutoff and no artificial match cap; the downstream bootstrap character budget owns content limiting.
- Preserve `fs.glob` no-match parity: a configured glob that matches nothing resolves to an empty set (not the literal pattern), so it no longer emits a phantom missing-file diagnostic; the literal `[pattern]` result is reserved for the no-glob-support fallback only.
- Suppress `closeFdAsync` rejections to avoid masking read errors on NFS/FUSE

**`src/hooks/internal-hooks.ts`** / **`src/hooks/internal-hook-dispatch.ts`**
- Keep the public `triggerInternalHook(event)` signature (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/hook-runtime`) unchanged and matching `main` — no new public parameter or exported options type.
- Move the bootstrap-only handler scheduling (`yieldBetweenHandlers` with `setImmediate` yield between handlers) and per-handler timing/slow-handler (>500ms) warning into an internal `internal-hook-dispatch` module that is not on the plugin SDK surface.

**`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.ts`**
- Instrument bootstrap-context substages (`workspace-file-load`, `hook-overrides`) with `performance.now` timing
- Log substage durations when total bootstrap-context exceeds 2 seconds
- Enable yielding between handlers for `agent:bootstrap` hook triggers (via the internal dispatch entrypoint)

**`src/agents/bootstrap-files.ts`** / **`src/agents/bootstrap-hooks.ts`**
- Keep the public `resolveBootstrapFilesForRun` params (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/agent-harness-runtime`) callback-free and matching `main`; route embedded-runner substage timing through an internal `resolveBootstrapFilesForRunWithTiming` variant kept off the SDK surface.
- Support the new async workspace file loading interface.

### Tests

- `workspace.test.ts` — 3 new tests for async fd read (happy path, cache hit, fd close on failure)
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — every matching file returned without an artificial cap (no directory pruning), and a regression test asserting a late-appearing match in a large tree is still loaded (no traversal cutoff)
- `handler.test.ts` — no truncation warning is emitted for large glob scans
- `internal-hooks.test.ts` — yield-between-handlers ordering, handler timing reporting, and slow handler warning exercised through the internal dispatch entrypoint
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — a no-match glob resolves to an empty set with no missing-file diagnostic (fs.glob parity)

The public plugin SDK surface is unchanged: `node scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs` exits 0 with no new package-exported entrypoints. All existing tests pass without modification.

### Performance impact

- Root bootstrap file loading: serial sync → parallel async (estimated 3-5x speedup for 8 files)
- Glob walks: synchronous/blocking → async with periodic `setImmediate` yields (prevents multi-second event-loop stalls on large workspaces). The walk completes fully; all configured matches are kept, and the existing bootstrap character-budget truncation handles content limiting.
- Hook chains: uninterrupted → yielded (prevents monopolizing the event loop during bootstrap)

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context loading caused by synchronous I/O and a blocking `fs.glob` walk over large workspaces, which blocks the loop and drops messages. This change makes the glob walk async/yielding so the loop stays responsive, while preserving every configured `bootstrap-extra-files` glob match (the earlier iteration of this branch added a hard 20,000-entry traversal cutoff that silently dropped late matches — that cutoff is removed here).
- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw checkout on macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`, run via `tsx` against the real exported `loadExtraBootstrapFiles` from `src/agents/workspace.ts`. Before/after captured from two git commits on the PR branch: before = `5849e709f4` (walker with the 20,000-entry cutoff), after = `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed).
- **Real environment scenario**: A workspace of ~26,100 filesystem entries (a 3-tier tree, 30×30×28 filler files) with a single configured-glob target `AGENTS.md` planted in the subtree the depth-first walker drains last, so the target is only reached after more than 20,000 visited entries. A 5ms repeating timer runs during the load as an event-loop liveness probe (steady ticks ⇒ the loop never stalled).
- **Failing proof before fix**: commit `5849e709f4` (cutoff present):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 82.9ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 16 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 0
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: false
  RESULT: late configured glob match was DROPPED (pre-fix behavior)
  ```
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  ```
  # against the patched checkout (commit 5ce395d645) a script that builds the
  # ~26,100-entry workspace, starts a 5ms liveness timer, then calls the real
  # loadExtraBootstrapFiles(root, ["**/AGENTS.md"]) and checks the deep match:
  npx tsx proof-live.mts
  ```
- **Evidence after fix**: terminal output from `node`/`tsx` against commit `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 99.4ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 20 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 1
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: true
  RESULT: configured glob match beyond old cutoff is PRESERVED; event loop stayed live
  ```
- **Observed result after fix**: With the cutoff removed, the configured `**/AGENTS.md` match located past the old 20,000-entry frontier is now loaded (1 file returned vs 0 before in the terminal output above), so existing broad `bootstrap-extra-files` configs no longer silently lose AGENTS.md/TOOLS.md context. The liveness timer kept ticking throughout the async walk (20 ticks during the ~99ms load), confirming the periodic `setImmediate` yields — not the cutoff — are what keep the event loop responsive.
- **What was not tested**: No full live `embedded_run` with active channel connections was driven end-to-end; this proof exercises the real glob-resolution code path and event-loop liveness directly rather than through a connected channel. The focused regression coverage lives in `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` and `handler.test.ts`.

Closes #87509

target.title: fix(tlon): bound urbit scry JSON response reads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Tlon Urbit scry reads (`/~/scry...`) could cause out-of-memory failures when the configured ship endpoint returns an oversized JSON body on the success path.

Poke operations already bounded error bodies with `readResponseTextLimited`, but scry success responses still used unbounded `response.json()`, so a hostile or misbehaving Urbit HTTP endpoint could stream arbitrarily large JSON into memory.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace the scry success-path `response.json()` call with the shared SDK helper `readProviderJsonResponse(response, "tlon.scry")`, which caps reads at 16 MiB and cancels the upstream stream on overflow. This closes the asymmetric bound on the Urbit channel-ops surface and aligns scry with the ongoing provider response-limit campaign.

Related focused PRs in the same plugin family: external image upload bounding (separate PR).

## User Impact

When Tlon scry reads ship state over HTTP, oversized JSON responses now fail fast with a bounded error instead of risking gateway/agent OOM. Normal small scry payloads behave unchanged.

## Evidence

Focused tests:

```text
pnpm test extensions/tlon/src/urbit/channel-ops.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose
```

Result: 3/3 passed, including malformed JSON rejection and a new ~18 MiB streaming regression at the 16 MiB cap.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Unbounded Urbit scry success JSON reads could OOM when the operator-configured ship endpoint streams an oversized body.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS, Node 22, Vitest with real `Response` / `ReadableStream` bodies (production `readProviderJsonResponse` path).
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
  1. `pnpm test extensions/tlon/src/urbit/channel-ops.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose`
- **Evidence after fix:**

```text
 ✓ parses successful scry JSON responses
 ✓ rejects malformed scry response JSON
 ✓ bounds oversized scry JSON responses

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  3 passed (3)
```

- **Observed result after fix:** Oversized scry JSON is rejected with `tlon.scry: JSON response exceeds 16777216 bytes`; valid small JSON still parses; malformed JSON surfaces `tlon.scry: malformed JSON response`.
- **What was not tested:** Live scry against a production Urbit ship; proof uses mocked `urbitFetch` returning real bounded `Response` streams.

## Tests and validation

- `pnpm test extensions/tlon/src/urbit/channel-ops.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose`
- Regression tests added/updated in `extensions/tlon/src/urbit/channel-ops.test.ts`

## Risk checklist

- Did user-visible behavior change? Yes — oversized scry responses now error instead of attempting unbounded buffering.
- Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? No
- Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? Yes — remote scry response handling is now bounded on the success path.
- Highest-risk area: Tlon channel operations that scry Urbit paths over HTTP.
- Mitigation: Shared 16 MiB provider JSON cap; stream cancelled on overflow; poke error-path bounding unchanged.

## Related context

Related #97558 (broader extensions JSON bounding batch — this PR is a focused scry-only slice using `readProviderJsonResponse`).

## Current review state

- Next action: awaiting maintainer review
- Bot comments addressed: none yet

## AI-assisted disclosure

- [x] AI-assisted (Cursor agent)
- [x] Human-run Real behavior proof from local setup
- [ ] `codex review --base upstream/main` (not run yet)

target.title: fix(gateway): redact Responses media blocks in chat history sanitization
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users viewing chat history in Control UI / WebChat would still receive embedded `data:` image payloads on Responses-style media blocks (`input_image.image_url` and legacy `image.url`) after history sanitization, even though other base64 and data-URL media paths were already redacted.

Also fixes CI failures in `chat.directive-tags.test.ts`: live WebChat broadcast must keep `{ type: "input_image", image_url: "data:..." }` for QR/image delivery, so inline media redaction is scoped to history-only paths.

## Why This Change Was Made

`sanitizeChatHistoryContentBlock()` now treats Responses media blocks the same as existing image/audio redaction when `redactInlineMedia: true` is passed from history paths only. Data URLs are removed from the projected history payload, replaced with `omitted: true` plus a byte count, while non-`data:` http(s) URLs remain intact for display/linking. Live broadcast via `projectChatDisplayMessages` keeps the default (`redactInlineMedia: false`) so inline images are preserved.

All chat.history-style callers now opt in: main gateway (`chat.ts`), session SSE snapshots (`session-history-state.ts`), embedded gateway stub, and TUI embedded backend.

## User Impact

Chat history fetched through the gateway, embedded agent tools, or TUI no longer leaks inline base64 image data for WebChat Responses `input_image` blocks or data-URL `image.url` blocks. Operators and users still see that media was present (via `omitted` + `bytes`) without shipping the raw payload over the wire. Remote https image links continue to display normally. Live WebChat broadcasts (QR codes, media replies) continue to deliver `input_image` data URLs to the client.

## Evidence

### Unit tests

```text
pnpm test src/gateway/server-methods/server-methods.test.ts -- -t "sanitizeChatHistoryMessages"
# 12 passed

# 90 passed

# 11 passed

pnpm test src/tui/embedded-backend.test.ts -- -t "embedded TUI history"
# 1 passed (redactInlineMedia asserted on loadHistory)
```

New/updated cases cover:
- sanitizer shapes: `input_image.image_url`, `image.url`, `image.source.data`, nested `image_url.url`, https preservation, broadcast preservation
- embedded gateway stub: all `chat.history` projection calls pass `redactInlineMedia: true`
- TUI embedded backend: `loadHistory` passes `redactInlineMedia: true` to `projectRecentChatDisplayMessages`

```text
node --import tsx scripts/proof-chat-history-sanitize-input-image.mjs
```

Test file: `src/gateway/server-methods/chat-history-inline-media-redaction-request.test.ts`

target.title: fix(boundary-safety): guard response reads and UTF-16 truncation
target.body:
## Summary

- Add a boundary safety guard that inventories existing raw UTF-16 text truncation and unbounded response-body reads, then blocks newly introduced production-file violations in changed-file checks.
- Wire the guard into `pnpm check`, `pnpm check:changed`, and package scripts with a baseline so existing debt stays visible without blocking unrelated PRs.
- Fix the shared response snippet helper and representative ACP/MiniMax/provider call sites to use bounded response reads and UTF-16-safe truncation.

## Origin / follow-up

Follow-up to #97620. That PR fixed one unbounded provider response-read path. This follow-up addresses the recurring root pattern behind the recent boundary-fix cluster by adding a CI guard for new high-confidence response-body and UTF-16 text-truncation bypasses instead of continuing to rely only on one-off call-site fixes.

## Competition / linked PR analysis

- #97620 is the direct source follow-up: it fixed one Google Meet Drive export bounded-read path, while this PR adds the guardrail intended to catch the same failure class when future production files change.
- #96264 is the focused MiniMax VLM success-response bound. This PR partially overlaps that call site, but it is broader: it adds the repository boundary-safety guard, baseline identity fix, JSON stdout contract, response snippet hardening, and representative bounded-read migrations.
- The MiniMax VLM success-response cap now aligns with the shared provider JSON cap at 16 MiB instead of introducing a narrower 4 MiB limit. That keeps the fail-closed behavior for oversized provider success JSON while reducing the compatibility disagreement called out by the related MiniMax-focused review path.
- If maintainers prefer #96264 as the canonical MiniMax-only route, the MiniMax hunk here can be reconciled or dropped while preserving the guard/baseline/tooling work that is unique to this PR.

## Maintainer-ready notes

- **Why it matters / User impact:** Recent boundary fixes have repeatedly patched individual channel/provider call sites for the same two failure classes: user-visible text truncated through raw UTF-16 code units, and external HTTP response bodies read without a byte cap. Without a guard, new provider/channel/plugin code can reintroduce the same failure class after the canonical helpers already exist.
- **Fix classification:** Root-cause CI/tooling guard for boundary safety regressions, plus small canonical-helper hardening.
- **Maintainer-ready confidence:** High for the local CI/tooling enforcement path and touched helper/call-site regressions. The proof is scoped to repository guard behavior and local `Response` stream boundaries, not remote service availability.
- **Root cause:** The source invariant was missing from CI: new production code could still bypass OpenClaw's canonical UTF-16 and bounded-response helpers even though those helpers existed. A few shared helpers and representative call sites also still contained raw response reads or raw head truncation, so the repository had no enforced contract that new boundary code must use the canonical owners.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** This root-cause fix enforces the missing repository invariant at the source: new production code must not introduce high-confidence raw UTF-16 head truncation or unbounded awaited `Response` body reads. `scripts/check-boundary-safety.mjs` scans production TypeScript with the TypeScript AST, compares findings to a checked-in baseline, and fails only on new changed-file violations. It catches high-confidence raw string head truncation and awaited external `Response` body reads while avoiding tests, fixtures, generated/vendor code, Express response writers, hash/protocol slices, and collection slicing. Baseline identity is stable across line-only movement by comparing file/rule/match counts instead of treating line numbers as part of the violation identity. `scripts/check-changed.mjs` runs the guard for core/extension changes, while `scripts/check.mjs` checks full baseline drift.
- **What did NOT change:** This does not rewrite all legacy baseline entries, add new public APIs, change response-size defaults outside the touched MiniMax success path, or modify credentials/configuration. Full legacy remediation and exhaustive taint analysis are out of scope.
- **Architecture / source-of-truth check:** `scripts/check-boundary-safety.mjs` is the source-of-truth validator for new boundary-safety violations; `test/fixtures/boundary-safety-inventory.json` is the baseline contract for current legacy inventory; `src/infra/http-body.ts` is the canonical bounded response/snippet helper for core runtime code; `openclaw/plugin-sdk/response-limit-runtime` exposes the bounded response reader to plugin code; `@openclaw/normalization-core/utf16-slice` remains the canonical UTF-16-safe truncation owner.
- **Patch quality notes:** The guard is intentionally high-confidence rather than exhaustive: it prevents new clear bypasses without forcing noisy legacy cleanup. After sync with current `origin/main`, the baseline contains 232 known entries; the earlier branch baseline dropped entries already fixed upstream and absorbed current main inventory drift. Related open PR scan found no open PR already adding these guard rule names.
- **Target test file:** `test/scripts/check-boundary-safety.test.ts`, `src/infra/http-body.response.test.ts`, `src/agents/minimax-vlm.boundary.test.ts`, `src/acp/control-plane/manager.test.ts`, `src/agents/tools/image-tool.test.ts`, `src/agents/tools/pdf-native-providers.test.ts`, and `src/media-understanding/image.test.ts`.
- **Scenario locked in:** New raw `messageText.slice(0, maxChars - 1)` text truncation is flagged; `truncateUtf16Safe(...)` is accepted; collection/hash/protocol slices are ignored; awaited `response.json()` / `res.text().catch(...)` reads are flagged; Express `res.json({...})` writers are ignored; a baseline-known finding remains accepted when only its line number moves; `--json` mode keeps stdout parseable while routing human status text to stderr; diagnostic snippets cancel exact-cap stalling streams; MiniMax tests now exercise real `Response` bodies for bounded JSON reads and prove a 5 MiB success JSON succeeds under the shared 16 MiB cap while a body over 16 MiB is canceled and rejected.
- **Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail:** The guard uses a baseline plus changed-file enforcement instead of a broad rewrite, so the test guardrail proves the invariant for new code while leaving legacy entries visible but non-blocking. It intentionally covers only high-confidence AST patterns and explains patch quality warnings from default returns/catches as fail-closed parser branches, not runtime fallbacks that mask user behavior.

## Root Cause

The root cause is a missing repository-level source invariant for boundary code. User-visible text can still be shortened with raw UTF-16 code-unit slicing, which can leave dangling surrogate halves when the cut lands inside an emoji or other surrogate-pair character. Remote HTTP responses can still be read with `response.json()`, `response.text()`, or `response.arrayBuffer()` directly, which buffers the entire body before OpenClaw can enforce the intended byte budget.

The canonical helpers existed, but the repository did not have a changed-file guard that forced new production code toward those helpers. As a result, each fix landed as a local call-site patch, while the next integration change could reintroduce the same boundary bypass in a sibling area. The shared response snippet path also still carried a raw no-stream fallback and raw character slicing, so even helper consumers were not fully protected.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** New production code that bypasses UTF-16-safe text truncation or bounded response-body helpers is now caught by the changed-file guard, while existing legacy findings remain tracked in a full-repo baseline. MiniMax VLM success JSON now uses the same bounded provider JSON reader with a 16 MiB cap, preserving normal provider-sized success responses while rejecting/canceling oversized bodies. After the conflict sync, the shared snippet path also cancels exact-cap diagnostic reads and no longer falls back to an unbounded `response.arrayBuffer()` path when no readable stream is available.
- **Real environment tested:** Local Linux OpenClaw repair worktree at `/media/vdb/code/ai/aispace/openclaw-worktrees/pr-97774`, branch `repair/pr-97774`, after syncing PR #97774 onto current `origin/main`. - **Proof request / real behavior evidence:** The reviewer-facing proof is mapped to the actual behavior changed here: repository guard execution, baseline diffing, and local `Response` stream boundary handling. No browser UI, hosted CI rerun, or remote MiniMax availability is claimed.
- **RF-001 — automation gate risk:** Verified against current main after the conflict sync: changed-file enforcement passes with 0 new entries, full baseline matches 232 entries, and `pnpm check:changed --dry-run` shows the guard is wired into the changed-file path. The remaining question is maintainer acceptance of the guard policy, not an unresolved merge conflict.
- **RF-002 — MiniMax success-response compatibility:** The MiniMax success path remains aligned to the shared 16 MiB provider JSON cap. The compatibility tradeoff for responses above 16 MiB is documented as fail-closed behavior and locked by `src/agents/minimax-vlm.boundary.test.ts`.
- **RF-003 — body-less HTTP error snippet overlap:** The conflict sync keeps the shared snippet helper bounded: standard readable `Response` streams are prefix-read and exact-cap diagnostic streams are canceled; non-readable/no-stream responses return no snippet rather than using an unbounded `response.arrayBuffer()` fallback. If maintainers prefer byte-clamped non-stream diagnostics from the sibling path, that is a policy choice outside this conflict repair.
- **RF-004 — maintainer policy boundary:** The remaining automation/compatibility questions are explicitly documented in the merge-risk section. This update resolves the merge conflict and current-head local verification without broadening scope into a new guard policy redesign.

## CI follow-up addressed

- **Current-head CI attribution:** The earlier compact-check failures on the previous head were current-PR direct regressions, not stale/main-baseline/infra failures. `checks-node-compact-small-whole-1` failed MiniMax/image-tool tests plus an exact-cap PDF error-body test; `checks-node-compact-large-whole-1` failed MiniMax media-understanding tests. Both failure classes line up with this PR's bounded MiniMax JSON reader and response-snippet boundary changes.
- **Fix applied:** MiniMax test fixtures now return real JSON `Response` bodies, with fresh bodies for multi-image calls, so the tests exercise the same bounded `Response.body` path as production. Diagnostic text snippets cancel exact-cap stalling streams, while `readResponseWithLimit` keeps its success-response overflow semantics. The conflict sync also keeps `src/infra/http-body.ts` free of the unbounded no-stream `arrayBuffer()` fallback flagged by the new guard.
- **Latest focused verification:** After syncing onto current `origin/main`, reran the guard checks, JSON stdout parse check, changed-check dry-run, boundary-safety tests, infra response-body tests, MiniMax boundary tests, ACP manager tests, image-tool tests, PDF provider tests, media-understanding image tests, `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm lint:scripts`, and `git diff --check`.

## Regression Test Plan

- `test/scripts/check-boundary-safety.test.ts` locks guard detection and false-positive boundaries for string truncation, response-body reads, Express writers, collection slices, baseline diffing, line-shift-stable baseline identity, and parseable `--json` stdout.
- `src/infra/http-body.response.test.ts` locks bounded response snippet behavior, UTF-16-safe snippet truncation, and exact-cap diagnostic stream cancellation.
- `src/agents/minimax-vlm.boundary.test.ts` locks success-response acceptance below the shared 16 MiB cap and overflow cancellation above the cap.
- `src/agents/tools/image-tool.test.ts` and `src/media-understanding/image.test.ts` lock MiniMax callers against real bounded JSON `Response` bodies instead of `.json()`-only mocks.
- `src/agents/tools/pdf-native-providers.test.ts` locks exact-cap provider error-body cancellation.
- `src/acp/control-plane/manager.test.ts` locks parented ACP task progress truncation without dangling surrogate halves.

## Merge risk

- **Risk labels considered:** CI/tooling, boundary safety, provider response reads, UTF-16 text truncation, provider compatibility.
- **Risk explanation:** The guard can block new changed-file code that uses raw response reads or raw string truncation in production files. It should not block unrelated legacy debt because existing entries are baseline-known by stable file/rule/match identity, not by fragile line numbers, and it intentionally excludes tests/fixtures/generated/vendor files plus common false positives. MiniMax VLM success responses over 16 MiB now fail closed through the bounded provider JSON reader instead of fully buffering the body.
- **Why acceptable:** The failure mode is actionable: use `truncateUtf16Safe`, `sliceUtf16Safe`, `readResponseWithLimit`, `readResponseTextSnippet`, `readProviderJsonResponse`, or add a narrow `boundary-safety-ignore <rule-id>: <reason>` for a proven false positive. This turns a repeated review/bug pattern into a local CI failure before PR submission. The MiniMax cap now matches the shared provider JSON response cap, so normal provider-sized success JSON has the same budget as other bounded provider JSON paths.
- **Out-of-scope boundary:** This PR does not attempt full legacy remediation, exhaustive taint analysis, or live third-party provider/channel validation.

target.title: fix(discord): disable ws 8.21.0 receiver part limits for gateway sockets
target.body:
## Summary

ws 8.21.0 introduced `maxBufferedChunks` and `maxFragments` receiver limits (commit `[security] Limit retained message parts`) that can trigger `WS_ERR_TOO_MANY_BUFFERED_PARTS` and close connections with code 1008 under certain traffic patterns.

This PR explicitly sets both limits to `0` (disabled) for Discord gateway WebSocket connections, restoring the ws 8.20.0 behavior for the trusted Discord gateway peer while preserving the security fix for all other WebSocket usage.

## Changes

- **`extensions/discord/src/internal/gateway.ts`**: Base class `createWebSocket()` now passes `maxBufferedChunks: 0, maxFragments: 0` with a `ws.ClientOptions` cast (since `@types/ws` 8.18.1 does not yet expose these fields).
- **`extensions/discord/src/monitor/gateway-plugin.ts`**: Extended `DiscordGatewayWebSocketCtor` type to include the new options; monitor gateway creation path passes the same disabled limits.
- **`extensions/discord/src/internal/gateway.test.ts`**: Added test verifying base class WebSocket receives the expected options.
- **`extensions/discord/src/monitor/gateway-plugin.test.ts`**: Added test verifying monitor plugin WebSocket receives the expected options.
- **`extensions/discord/src/monitor/provider.proxy.test.ts`**: Updated two existing exact-match assertions to include the new options.

## Why `0` instead of raising the limits

- ws 8.21.0 treats `0` as disabled (`receiver.js:61`, `receiver.js:98`: `if (this._maxBufferedChunks > 0 && ...)`), matching the pre-8.21.0 behavior exactly.
- Discord gateway is a trusted peer; the security limits are designed to protect against untrusted senders.
- Choosing an arbitrary higher threshold would be fragile without real production traffic data to calibrate against.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: ws 8.21.0's retained-part receiver limits (`maxFragments` default 131072 / `maxBufferedChunks` default 1048576) abort a Discord gateway socket with `WS_ERR_TOO_MANY_BUFFERED_PARTS` / close `1008`; this PR sets both to `0` (disabled) on the Discord gateway sockets, restoring ws 8.20.0 behavior for that trusted peer.
- **Real environment tested**: Live Discord gateway connection from a Docker `node:22-bookworm-slim` container (Node `v22.22.3`) with the repo-pinned `ws@8.21.0` installed exactly, using a real bot token (redacted), connecting to `wss://gateway.discord.gg/?v=10&encoding=json`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**: build a `node:22-bookworm-slim` image with `npm install ws@8.21.0`, then run a client that constructs the gateway socket with this patch's options (`new ws.WebSocket(url, { handshakeTimeout: 30000, maxBufferedChunks: 0, maxFragments: 0 })`), completes the HELLO/IDENTIFY/READY handshake against the real Discord gateway, sends heartbeats, holds a 60s stable window, then closes with code 1000.
- **Evidence after fix**: Live Discord gateway run with this patch's options applied (token, `session_id`, and `resume_gateway_url` redacted):

```
[env] node=v22.22.3 ws=8.21.0
[discord] connecting wss://gateway.discord.gg (maxBufferedChunks:0, maxFragments:0)
[discord] open
[discord] HELLO heartbeat_interval=41250ms
[discord] IDENTIFY sent (token redacted)
[discord] READY received (session_id/resume_gateway_url redacted)
[discord] HEARTBEAT_ACK #1
[discord] stable window 60000ms complete
[discord] close code=1000 reason=<empty>
[result] PASS live: READY + 1 heartbeat ACK; no WS_ERR_TOO_MANY_BUFFERED_PARTS during stable window
```

Supplemental deterministic mechanism repro against a local ws 8.21.0 gateway streaming one message in 131073 fragments (one over the client default `maxFragments`), exercising the same `ws.WebSocket` receiver path:

```
# default ws.WebSocket (ws 8.21 defaults)
[before] open
[before] error code=WS_ERR_TOO_MANY_BUFFERED_PARTS message=Too many message fragments
[before] close code=1006 reason=<empty>

# this patch's options applied
[after] open
[after] message received: 131073 bytes - NO receiver-limit close
```

- **Observed result after fix**: On the real Discord gateway, with the disabled limits applied, the connection reaches `READY`, exchanges heartbeats, and stays connected through the 60s window with no `WS_ERR_TOO_MANY_BUFFERED_PARTS` and no `1008` close; the only close is the intentional client-initiated `1000`. The deterministic repro confirms the same constructor options remove the receiver-limit close that the default ws 8.21 client hits.
- **What was not tested**: the live run confirms a real gateway session stays healthy with the patched options, but does not force Discord's production fragmentation pattern on demand, does not exercise the `zlib-stream` transport, and does not drive the full OpenClaw plugin wiring end-to-end. The deterministic repro proves the ws 8.21 retained-part mechanism and that this patch's options disable the exact receiver checks, but uses a local peer rather than Discord's live framing.

## Tests

- `gateway.test.ts`: 25 passed
- `gateway-plugin.test.ts`: 17 passed  
- `provider.proxy.test.ts`: 21 passed
- TypeScript check (tsgo): clean

Fixes #88330

target.title: [AI-assisted] Add session history family lookup
target.body:
## Problem

When a threaded conversation has already been split across reset transcripts, `chat.history` and the `sessions_history` tool only read the currently active transcript. The session store can already retain the family through `usageFamilySessionIds`, but history readers do not use that chain and do not discover archived `*.jsonl.reset.<timestamp>` topic transcripts.

That means an agent/tool can be looking at the correct logical Telegram/Slack/Discord thread and still miss earlier turns after session rollover.

## Fix

Add an opt-in family history path:

- `chat.history` accepts `includeFamily: true`.
- `sessions_history` accepts `includeFamily`.
- Gateway and embedded `chat.history` now share the bounded/header-checked reset archive resolver instead of using separate prefix scans.
- The shared resolver can include owned topic-suffixed reset archives such as `<sessionId>-topic-456.jsonl.reset.<timestamp>` only when the archive header matches the requested session id.
- Same-prefix colliding topic archives and headerless topic archives are ignored.
- Family read targets are capped before transcript reads, and normal `chat.history` behavior remains opt-in: UI startup does not load ancestor history.

## Validation

Current head: `1aa4e9cbb94f6841803bd55559aa0ea6de17dc67`.

## Real Behavior Proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** A logical thread whose active session has `usageFamilySessionIds` should be able to fetch earlier reset transcript turns when a caller explicitly requests family history, including owned topic-suffixed reset archives, without reading colliding or headerless topic archives. The current active transcript must also be preserved when a retained reset family has more entries than the bounded 32 read targets.
- **Real environment tested:** Local OpenClaw checkout on this PR branch at current head `a12e1bbcf0`, using temporary on-disk session directories, the real Gateway `chat.history` RPC integration harness, embedded-mode `chat.history`, and the same reset archive filename/header patterns that OpenClaw creates for topic transcripts.

  1. Created temporary session directories and session-store entries with `usageFamilySessionIds` linking an ancestor session and the current session.
  2. Wrote an owned plain ancestor reset archive and an owned topic-suffixed ancestor archive with matching `type: "session"` headers.
  3. Wrote newer same-prefix colliding and headerless topic reset archives in the same sessions directory.
  4. Invoked the real Gateway `chat.history` RPC path with and without `includeFamily: true`.
  5. Created a second Gateway/RPC case with 40 ancestor session ids before the current id in `usageFamilySessionIds`.

- **Observed result after fix:** Default `chat.history` excludes ancestor reset archive content, while `chat.history(includeFamily)` includes the owned plain ancestor archive, includes the owned topic-suffixed ancestor archive, includes current-session content, and rejects the colliding/headerless topic reset archives. In the >32-target Gateway/RPC regression, `chat.history(includeFamily)` contains `current survives family target cap`, contains early ancestor content, and does not read the ancestor entries beyond the target cap. Embedded `chat.history(includeFamily)` now reads the current active transcript first, then current archives, then ancestor archives/active transcripts; its >32-target regression also keeps the current transcript and drops over-cap ancestors.

target.title: fix: antml:/mm: namespaced tool-call XML leaks into chat replies (#97750)
target.body:
Closes #97750

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users on any deployment that serves a Claude model through an anthropic-messages-compatible proxy would see raw tool-call XML in their chat replies, and sometimes get no usable answer at all, when the proxy intermittently degraded a native `tool_use` block into plain text.

In that degraded case the model's tool call arrives as the Anthropic namespaced XML dialect — an optional `function_calls` wrapper containing `antml:invoke` / `antml:parameter` tags that use `name="..."` attributes (MiniMax emits the same shape with an `mm:` prefix). The harness did not recognize the namespace prefix or the attribute form anywhere, so the entire block leaked into the user-visible message instead of being executed, and a turn whose whole body was unrecognized markup could end with no real reply.

A follow-up fix in this PR also closes a streaming-only variant of the same leak: the final repair parser accepts whitespace-flexible attribute-dialect invoke tags (optional whitespace after `<`, around the `name` attribute, and around `=`), but the streamed-prefix recognizer only kept the exact `<ns>invoke name="` form buffered. A grammar-legal split form such as `<invoke name = "exec">` was therefore classified impossible mid-stream and flushed as raw visible text before final-message repair could promote it.

## Why This Change Was Made

The degraded tool call should never reach the user: it should either be executed or, failing that, hidden. This change teaches both layers that own that contract about the namespaced attribute dialect, using a closed namespace allow-list (`antml:`, `mm:`) factored into a single reused fragment — mirroring the existing reasoning-tag handling — so arbitrary `ns:` prefixes are not matched.

- Visible-text sanitizer: the tag-name scan now skips a known namespace prefix before reading the local tag name, and the quick-check / payload-start patterns accept the same optional prefix, so a namespaced wrapper is stripped on the same opt-in paths as the bare dialect.
- Repair/promotion layer: the repair grammar now promotes the attribute dialect (`invoke name="..."` / `parameter name="..."`, optionally namespaced, optionally wrapped in `function_calls`) back into an executed tool call, including the streaming and over-cap paths. Parameterless/self-closing invokes are never promoted, parameter values stay literal, and the existing payload-size limits are honored.
- Streaming-prefix recognizer: `isViableXmlishInvokeOpenPrefix` is rewritten as a phase scanner that mirrors the final parser grammar one token at a time, so a buffer that ends partway through any phase of a grammar-legal invoke open (including whitespace-split forms) stays buffered instead of leaking, while the existing tool-name gating is preserved unchanged.
- `stripPlainTextToolCallBlocks` gained an optional code-region predicate, threaded in from the delivery pipeline and `sanitizeUserFacingText`, so a complete invoke block inside a fenced or inline code span is no longer silently removed.

Non-goals/boundaries: the Anthropic and DSML transports are intentionally untouched (the native path is correct; the failure is degraded text owned by the repair package and sanitizer), no new public SDK surface is added, and no runtime fallback execution from sanitized text is introduced. The equals dialect (`<function=...>`/`<parameter=...>`), bracket, and Harmony paths are unchanged.

## User Impact

Users on proxied Claude routes no longer see raw `antml:` tool-call XML in their replies. When the proxy degrades a tool call to text, the call is now recovered and executed instead of leaking, so the turn produces a real result. This now also holds when the degraded tool call streams in a whitespace-flexible form split across chunks, which previously slipped past the streamed-prefix recognizer and leaked. Code examples that legitimately contain such tags inside code fences or inline code are preserved rather than stripped.

## Evidence

Focused unit tests cover both layers and the edge cases:

- Sanitizer: namespaced `function_calls`/`invoke`/`parameter` stripped to surrounding prose; truncated namespaced opening hidden; namespaced markup preserved inside fenced and inline code through the full delivery pipeline. Delivery-path regression coverage locks both directions across the `antml:`, `mm:`, and bare (no-namespace) prefixes: an unfenced standalone `invoke` block (and a pure standalone block with no surrounding prose) is stripped, while the same block inside a fenced code span is preserved verbatim, so the real leak shape is removed without over-scrubbing legitimate code examples.
- Promotion: a streamed namespaced attribute-dialect message promotes to a real tool call (including a split/chunked stream); a self-closing parameterless invoke is not promoted; mixed prose declines promotion; an arbitrary `foo:` namespace is neither promoted nor stripped (locks the closed allow-list); multiple invokes in one wrapper parse and strip correctly; a parameter value containing a literal close marker is extracted to the first close.
- Streaming-prefix recognizer: whitespace-split attribute-dialect invoke opens (spaces around the `name` attribute and `=`, including the open tag split across stream chunks at the whitespace boundaries, for both `antml:` and bare namespaces and a single-quote variant) stay buffered and promote to a tool call instead of leaking.
- Argument-less invoke followed by prose: a complete zero-parameter (`<invoke name="read"></invoke>\nHello`) or self-closing (`<invoke name="read"/>\nHello`) invoke followed by visible prose no longer leaks the raw invoke XML in streamed output — the invoke markup is stripped and only the prose (`Hello`) is delivered, with no tool call promoted, across `antml:`, `mm:`, and bare prefixes and split-across-chunks streams. Regression coverage also locks the final-message shapes where the invoke and prose arrive as separate text content blocks, and where a single leading content block carries both the invoke and its trailing prose, so the visible prose is preserved exactly once with no duplication or loss; a pure argument-less invoke with no prose still scrubs to an empty message; and a parametered invoke with no prose still promotes to a tool call (positive lock).

Real-behavior proof (Docker, redacted): a self-contained harness under `proof/pr-97845/` drives the actual stream normalizer through the same option wiring the provider-stream wrapper uses, feeding a degraded provider stream that emits a whitespace-split invoke open (`<invoke name = "exec">...`) split across chunks at the whitespace boundaries. Captured runtime output shows the regression and its fix:

With the recognizer reverted to its previous literal-prefix form (BEFORE), the split open leaks as visible text:

```
fake upstream chunks: ["<invoke"," name"," ="," \"exec\">","<parameter name=\"command\">echo demo</parameter>","</invoke>"]
emitted events:
  [1] text_delta "<invoke"
  [2] text_delta " name"
  [3] text_delta " ="
  [4] text_delta " \"exec\">"
  [5] text_delta "<parameter name=\"command\">echo demo</parameter>"
  [6] text_delta "</invoke>"
  [7] toolcall_start ...
visible text emitted to user: "<invoke name = \"exec\"><parameter name=\"command\">echo demo</parameter></invoke>"
VERDICT: LEAK
```

With the fix in place (AFTER), the same bytes stay buffered and promote to a tool call with no visible leak:

```
emitted events:
  [0] toolcall_start
  [1] toolcall_delta {"command":"echo demo"}
  [2] done reason=toolUse  toolCall name=exec arguments={"command":"echo demo"}
visible text emitted to user: ""
VERDICT: NO LEAK
```

The captured output above is the redacted before/after runtime evidence; the synthetic stream reproduction needs no provider key. (The proof was produced with a Docker harness that drives the real stream normalizer through the provider-stream wrapper; per review feedback it is kept here in the description rather than committed to the branch.)

Local validation:

```
node scripts/test-projects.mjs (affected test files): pass (sanitizer + promotion + agents)
vitest src/plugin-sdk/provider-stream-shared.test.ts: 92 pass (incl. new whitespace-split and argument-less-invoke-plus-prose regressions)
pnpm tsgo:core && pnpm tsgo:core:test: clean
oxlint on changed source files: 0 warnings, 0 errors
oxfmt --check on changed files: all correctly formatted
```

target.title: feat(android): reconnect gateway when validated network returns
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When Android loses and regains network connectivity, the OpenClaw Android app could remain disconnected from the gateway until the user foregrounded the app or the `GatewaySession` backoff timer expired. That left node/operator sessions offline longer than necessary after Wi‑Fi/cellular recovery.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add a small `NetworkMonitor` that listens for validated transport restoration via `ConnectivityManager.registerNetworkCallback` (same default `NetworkRequest` pattern as `GatewayDiscovery`) and calls the existing `reconnectPreferredGatewayOnForeground()` path.

Design constraints:

- **Zero new permissions**: `ACCESS_NETWORK_STATE` is already declared in `AndroidManifest.xml`.
- **Zero config/compat surface**: no SecurePrefs, config, env, loopback, or command-registry changes.
- **Reuse existing guards**: `reconnectPreferredGatewayOnForeground()` already skips when connected, when a gateway trust decision is pending, and otherwise refreshes or reconnects via stored/preferred endpoint resolution.
- **Validated-only signal**: both `onAvailable` and `onCapabilitiesChanged` require `NET_CAPABILITY_VALIDATED` before emitting, so captive-portal/unvalidated networks do not trigger premature reconnects.
- **Deduped transitions**: offline→online emits once; capability churn while online is suppressed; `onLost` clears state so a later restore can emit again.

This is upstream of the offline/reconnect-behavior PR series (#100267 / #100277 / #100290 / #100301 / #100219 / #100227 / #100331): those changes assume a reconnect has happened and improve post-reconnect behavior; this PR makes reconnect happen sooner after transport recovery.

## User Impact

After network drops and comes back, Android should reconnect to the preferred gateway faster without requiring a manual foreground nudge, while avoiding reconnect storms during routine capability churn.

## Evidence

- `apps/android/app/src/test/java/ai/openclaw/app/gateway/NetworkMonitorTest.kt` — pure JUnit coverage for the dedupe state machine (first emit, duplicate suppress, lost→online re-emit).

Local Gradle unit proof:

```powershell
$env:ANDROID_SDK_ROOT = "F:\Android\Sdk"
```

## What Problem This Solves

Apple Watch quick replies were accepted in memory and could be lost when the iOS app was offline, suspended, or terminated before Gateway delivery. Delayed WatchConnectivity fallbacks could also duplicate delivery or route a reply after the active Gateway changed.

This supersedes #100031 after GitHub auto-closed the contributor branch during a maintainer ancestry repair. The implementation and contributor attribution are preserved here so the reviewed fix can land cleanly.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Reuse the existing durable, gateway-scoped Watch message outbox instead of maintaining a second reply queue.
- Persist accepted messages before awaiting delivery and use `chat.send` idempotency keys.
- Carry source-Gateway identity through Watch notifications and persist bounded prompt routes for released Watch builds.
- Persist bounded delivery tombstones to deduplicate delayed fallbacks across process restarts.
- Serialize flushes, prioritize replies, revalidate Gateway identity before every send, and retain bounded transient retries.
- Preserve current Watch chat/voice behavior while quick replies finish without waiting for spoken completion.

## User Impact

Watch quick replies survive iPhone process loss and reconnects, avoid duplicate sends, and never guess across Gateways. Existing `watch.chat.command.queue.v1` data remains decodable.

target.title: feat(control-ui): session grouping with drag & drop and channel categorization
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Control UI sessions table is a flat list. Once an operator runs many sessions across agents and message channels (Discord, Telegram, WhatsApp, ...), there is no way to organize them: no grouping, no way to categorize channel-originated sessions, and no equivalent of the desktop app's custom session groups.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds a persistent per-session `category` field end-to-end (gateway protocol `sessions.patch` -> session store -> list rows -> live session-change events) and a "Group by" control on the web Sessions page with None / Custom groups / Channel / Kind / Agent / Date modes. The field is named `category` to stay clearly separate from the existing chat-group concepts (`groupId`, `groupChannel`, kind `group`). Custom group membership persists server-side on the session entry; empty just-created groups live in browser localStorage until a session is assigned. Cleared categories emit an explicit `null` in session events so other connected clients drop the group during merge-reconcile instead of going stale.

## User Impact

- Group the sessions table by custom groups, channel, kind, agent, or date, with section headers and counts; the chosen mode persists per browser.
- Create custom groups and assign sessions by dragging rows onto a section (drop-target highlight), or via a per-row group selector; sessions from message channels can be categorized like any other session.
- Channel mode buckets sessions by their originating channel out of the box.
- Group names are searchable in the table filter and shown in the session details panel.

target.title: fix(msteams): handle bot removal and uninstallation to mark sessions stale
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Microsoft Teams users who remove and re-add the OpenClaw bot would retain access to previous DM conversation history. After a user removed and re-added the bot in a personal chat, OpenClaw resumed the same server-side DM session without an explicit retention decision, creating a privacy concern.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add `onMembersRemoved` and `onInstallationUpdate` handlers to detect when the bot is removed or uninstalled from personal DM conversations. When either event occurs, the handlers now:
1. Identify the affected user's session keys using the format `agent:<accountId>:msteams:direct:<userId>`
2. Mark all matching sessions as stale by atomically setting `updatedAt` to 0
3. Preserve transcript records while signaling that new sessions should be created on the next message

The implementation follows the same pattern used in Discord's thread-session-close.ts and ensures proper privacy boundaries when users reinstall the bot.

Two new activity handlers are added:
- `onMembersRemoved`: Detects when the bot is removed from personal DM conversations
- `onInstallationUpdate`: Handles app installation/uninstallation events in personal chats

Both handlers use atomic session updates via `patchSessionEntry` to prevent race conditions and include appropriate error handling.

## User Impact

Microsoft Teams users can now expect proper privacy boundaries when removing and re-adding the OpenClaw bot. Previous DM conversation history will not be automatically accessible after reinstallation, aligning with user privacy expectations and Teams platform behavior.

## Evidence

The fix modifies two files:
- `extensions/msteams/src/monitor-handler.ts`: Adds handler implementations for membersRemoved and installationUpdate activities (+204 lines)
- `extensions/msteams/src/monitor.ts`: Extends the activity handler type definition and routing logic (+18 lines)

The implementation has been verified through code review against the existing session management infrastructure and follows established patterns from other channels (Discord).

Closes #99054

target.title: fix(agents): broadcast agent stream=thinking to gateway clients without channel callback (supersedes #79687)
target.body: ## Summary Decouple `streamReasoning` from the optional `onReasoningStream` channel callback so `chat.send`-originated runs (webchat / Control UI / WebSocket / ACP / cron auto-reply / heartbeat) receive live `agent.stream === "thinking"` events when `reasoningMode === "stream"`. Supersedes #79687, #47613. Closes #42261, #5086. ## Type of change - [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [x] Documentation update - [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) - [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected) ## Why this is needed On `upstream/main` (`src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe.ts:146-150`), `streamReasoning` is gated on `typeof params.onReasoningStream === "function"`. Telegram / Mattermost integrations supply that callback, so they get live thinking; every other surface that goes through `chat.send` (webchat, Control UI, plain WS clients, ACP, cron auto-reply, heartbeats) does **not** supply a callback, so `emitReasoningStream` short-circuits before reaching `emitAgentEvent`. The result is the symptom reported in #42261 and #5086: agents look frozen during reasoning for every non-Telegram subscriber. This has been attempted multiple times before (#47613, #52642, #61469, #79687, #80543, #80956). #79687 is the most complete prior attempt — ClawSweeper judged its patch correct (0.86 confidence); the only outstanding gap was that `docs/tools/thinking.md` still described `/reasoning stream` as Telegram-only. This PR carries that doc fix in the same commit, plus regression tests that #47613 was missing, so the entire surface is closed in one PR. ## What changed ### Runtime - `src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe.ts` - `streamReasoning` now requires only `reasoningMode === "stream" && canShowReasoning`. The optional channel callback no longer participates in the gate. - `emitReasoningStream` no longer early-returns when `onReasoningStream` is absent; the callback is invoked with optional chaining when supplied. ### Documentation - `docs/tools/thinking.md` - Replace the "Telegram only" note with the actual cross-client behavior. - Document the `thinkingLevel: "off"` hard-gate guarantee explicitly. - `docs/channels/telegram.md` - Drop the "Telegram-only reasoning stream" framing. - Add a pointer back to the canonical reasoning-visibility section. ### Tests - `src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe.subscribe-embedded-agent-session.subscribeembeddedagentsession.test.ts` - 4 new regression tests under a new `describe("agent stream=thinking emission without onReasoningStream callback")`: 1. broadcasts `agent stream=thinking` to gateway clients with no callback supplied (covers chat.send / WS / webchat / ACP / cron paths) 2. does not leak reasoning when `thinkingLevel` is `"off"` even without a callback (visibility hard-gate) 3. respects `silentExpected` and emits no thinking events even without a callback 4. still invokes `onReasoningStream` when supplied (Telegram / Mattermost path remains unchanged) ## Visibility / safety guarantees preserved - `streamReasoning` still requires `canShowReasoning`, so `thinkingLevel: "off"` continues to **hard-disable** the broadcast — opting out of thinking still blocks the live thinking stream. This is what #47613 missed and is one of the reasons that PR was closed. - `silentExpected` runs (heartbeat probes etc.) still suppress the broadcast. - `onReasoningStream` is now optional: Telegram / Mattermost integrations still receive the callback exactly as before when they supply it. ## How this addresses prior PR blockers | Prior PR | Reason it was closed | How this PR resolves it | | --- | --- | --- | | #79687 | ClawSweeper said patch is correct (0.86); only gap was `docs/tools/thinking.md` not matching the new runtime behavior. No human maintainer approval, no assignee. | Doc fix is included in the same commit. PR description carries `Real behavior proof` directly so the proof gate passes. | | #47613 | (a) missing `canShowReasoning` gate after rebase — could leak reasoning when `thinkingLevel:"off"`; (b) no Gateway/WebSocket regression tests; (c) `docs/tools/thinking.md` still Telegram-only. | (a) `canShowReasoning` is preserved on line 146; (b) 4 new tests cover no-callback / thinkingLevel:"off" / silentExpected / Telegram callback paths; (c) doc fix included. | | #42261, #5086 | Closed as duplicate / not planned by triage bots, not on technical merit. | Linked via `Closes` so they auto-close on merge. | ## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs) - Behavior or issue addressed: When `/reasoning stream` is active and `chat.send` is invoked **without** an `onReasoningStream` callback (the path used by webchat / Control UI / plain WebSocket / ACP / cron auto-reply / heartbeat), the gateway broadcasts `agent.stream === "thinking"` events on the agent event bus as the model thinks. Each event carries `runId`, `data.text` (cumulative reasoning), and `data.delta` (incremental). On `upstream/main`, the same path emits zero thinking events because `streamReasoning` short-circuits when `onReasoningStream` is undefined. - Real environment tested: - OS: macOS 14 - Node: v22 - pnpm: 10.32.1 - OpenClaw: `upstream/main` @ HEAD with this branch (`fix/reasoning-stream-supersede-79687`) applied - Test runner: `vitest` via `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` with `test/vitest/vitest.agents-core.config.ts` - End-to-end client: a downstream Electron WebSocket client subscribed to the gateway agent event bus - Exact steps or command run after this patch: 1. Check out `upstream/main`, apply this branch, run `pnpm install`. 2. Run the new regression suite scoped to the no-callback path: ``` node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run \ --config test/vitest/vitest.agents-core.config.ts \ src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe.subscribe-embedded-agent-session.subscribeembeddedagentsession.test.ts \ -t "agent stream=thinking emission without onReasoningStream callback" ``` 3. For end-to-end, start the gateway, send a `chat.send` directive `/reasoning stream`, then send a normal user prompt that requires reasoning. 4. Observe the agent event bus on a non-Telegram WebSocket subscriber. 5. Repeat with `thinkingLevel: "off"` to confirm the visibility hard-gate. - Evidence after fix: Terminal capture of the new regression suite (`4 passed | 39 skipped`): End-to-end capture of a non-Telegram WebSocket client rendering streamed thinking inline (`agent.stream === "thinking"` events delivered before final assistant text): - Observed result after fix: - Step 2: `4 passed | 39 skipped` — covers no-callback emission, `thinkingLevel:"off"` suppression, `silentExpected` suppression, and the existing Telegram callback path. - Step 3: the WebSocket client receives `agent.stream === "thinking"` events incrementally and renders them inline before any final assistant text is sent. - Step 4: zero `agent.stream === "thinking"` events are emitted when thinking is disabled, confirming the `thinkingLevel:"off"` gate remains intact. - What was not tested: - Live Telegram channel: author does not have channel credentials. The new regression test `still invokes onReasoningStream when supplied` plus the unchanged Telegram code path should keep that surface safe. - Live Mattermost channel: same as Telegram. - ACP transport end-to-end: covered at the unit level via the no-callback `chat.send` test, not against a real ACP client. - Cron auto-reply end-to-end: covered at the unit level via the no-callback test, not against a live cron run. ## Backwards compatibility - Telegram / Mattermost: unchanged — they still pass `onReasoningStream` and still get the callback. The Telegram preview-bubble UX described in `docs/channels/telegram.md` is unchanged. - `chat.send` / WebSocket / webchat / Control UI / ACP / cron auto-reply / heartbeat: previously received zero thinking events when `/reasoning stream` was active; now receive `agent.stream === "thinking"` events on the agent event bus. This is additive behavior gated behind an existing opt-in directive. - Users who do not opt in to `/reasoning stream` (default `off`, or `on` for non-streamed thinking blocks) see no behavior change. - `thinkingLevel: "off"` still hard-disables thinking on every surface, including this stream. ## Test plan - [x] `vitest` agents-core suite passes locally (`43 passed`, including 4 new cases). - [x] Lint clean (`oxlint` runs in pre-commit hook, no findings). - [x] Manual end-to-end against a downstream WS client confirms `agent.stream === "thinking"` events arrive incrementally with both `text` (cumulative) and `delta` (incremental) populated. - [x] Manual end-to-end with `thinkingLevel: "off"` confirms zero thinking events are emitted (visibility gate intact). - [ ] CI: full agents test matrix (delegated to GitHub Actions). ## Risk / rollback Runtime change is 1 expression rewrite + 1 optional-chaining call. If a regression surfaces in Telegram / Mattermost, reverting just `src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe.ts` restores prior behavior; the doc and test changes are independently safe to keep. ## Reviewer notes - The runtime diff is intentionally minimal — same shape as #79687, plus the doc fix that was its only ClawSweeper blocker, plus the regression tests that #47613 was closed for missing. - Happy to add ACP / cron-specific integration tests if reviewers want explicit coverage at those surfaces, but the new unit tests already exercise the exact code path those surfaces hit (`chat.send` without `onReasoningStream`). - Author has limited ability to test Telegram / Mattermost end-to-end; the existing Telegram callback test (#4 above) plus the unchanged Telegram code path should keep that surface safe, but a maintainer with channel credentials confirming live behavior would be appreciated. ## Linked issues Closes #42261 Closes #5086 Related #79687 Related #47613

target.title: fix(anthropic): configure undici Agent with extended keep-alive to prevent socket failures
target.body:
## What changed

This fix configures Anthropic provider to use a custom undici Agent with extended keep-alive timeout, preventing socket failures on long-running gateways.

**Root cause**: The Anthropic SDK uses undici with default `keepAliveTimeout` of 4 seconds. After 1-3 hours of uptime, idle keep-alive connections get closed by network infrastructure, causing `UND_ERR_SOCKET` errors on subsequent requests. These errors are classified as `timeout` and trigger the fallback chain, silently swapping to a fallback model mid-conversation.

**Solution**: Create a custom undici Agent with:
- `keepAliveTimeout: 60_000` (60s vs default 4s)
- `connectTimeout: 15_000` (15s)
- `bodyTimeout: 600_000` (10min)
- `allowH2: false` (disable HTTP/2 for compatibility)
- `connections: 20` (limit per origin)
- `pipelining: 4` (better throughput)

Apply this Agent to all Anthropic client variants via `fetchOptions.dispatcher`.

## Why

The issue (#87407) reports real production occurrences where users saw "LLM request rejected" errors with internal API path references, and the agent silently switched models mid-turn. This is a poor user experience and makes debugging difficult. By extending keep-alive timeouts, we reduce the chance of socket keep-alive timeouts on established connections, preventing unnecessary fallbacks.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: UND_ERR_SOCKET keep-alive failures causing silent mid-turn fallback to secondary models.

**Real environment tested**: Local OpenClaw checkout, Node.js 24.x, TypeScript compilation verified.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

```bash
# Build and type-check
pnpm build:ci-artifacts

# Run focused tests related to Anthropic provider
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/llm/providers/anthropic.test.ts

# Run autoreview (if available)
# /Users/steipete/Projects/agent-scripts/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode branch --base origin/main
```

**Evidence after fix**: Build succeeds without errors. Anthropic provider tests pass (refer to CI results).

**Observed result after fix**: The Anthropic client now uses a custom undici Agent with extended `keepAliveTimeout` of 60 seconds. This prevents idle socket closures that previously caused `UND_ERR_SOCKET` errors during long-running sessions. The connection pool is configured with conservative timeouts and limits.

**What was not tested**: 
- Live multi-hour uptime stress test 
- Real Anthropic API credential testing (requires production deployment)
- HTTP/2 behavior (explicitly disabled)
- Specific network conditions that caused original failures (requires reproducer access)

**Verification**: This change should be validated in a staging/production environment by monitoring for the absence of `UND_ERR_SOCKET` errors in gateway logs over extended uptime periods when using Anthropic providers.

target.title: fix(codex): project MCP OAuth config
target.body:
## Summary

What problem does this PR solve?

- OpenClaw-owned remote MCP server config could not carry the OAuth descriptors Codex needs for OAuth-capable remote MCP servers.
- As a result, users could configure a remote MCP server in `mcp.servers`, but the Codex harness projection could not preserve the OAuth resource/client metadata needed for Codex to treat that server as auth-capable.

Why does this matter now?

- Codex-backed OpenClaw users increasingly add remote MCP servers through OpenClaw-native `mcp.servers` config. OAuth metadata should stay on that OpenClaw surface instead of requiring users to maintain a separate Codex config.

What is the intended outcome?

- Remote MCP servers may declare `oauth_resource` and optional `oauth.client_id`.
- Codex MCP projection includes those fields for remote URL-backed servers.
- Stdio MCP servers never receive Codex-unsupported OAuth fields.

What is intentionally out of scope?

- Changing Codex's OAuth flow.
- Adding provider-specific Composio logic.
- Changing non-Codex MCP projection behavior.

What does success look like?

- OpenClaw config accepts remote MCP OAuth descriptors, projects them into Codex thread start/resume config, and keeps stdio server projection unchanged.

What should reviewers focus on?

- Config compatibility for `mcp.servers`.
- Codex-only projection behavior.
- Stdio omission of OAuth fields.
- Thread start/resume lifecycle coverage.

AI-assisted: yes. I used Codex to implement and review the change, then ran the checks and real-environment proof below.

## Linked context

Which issue does this close?

N/A

Which issues, PRs, or discussions are related?

N/A

Was this requested by a maintainer or owner?

No maintainer request. This came from testing OpenClaw's Codex harness with remote OAuth MCP servers.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

- Behavior addressed: OpenClaw `mcp.servers` remote MCP config can now carry OAuth metadata through the Codex harness projection.
- Real environment tested: macOS Mac mini running OpenClaw with Codex CLI `0.134.0`, using an OpenClaw agent Codex home and a real Composio remote MCP server at `https://connect.composio.dev/mcp`.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch: built this branch in a temporary checkout, used the patched projection path against the real OpenClaw config, verified Codex saw the remote MCP server as OAuth-capable, completed `codex mcp login` with `CODEX_HOME` set to the OpenClaw agent Codex home, then called the remote MCP endpoint with the resulting credential.
- Evidence after fix (screenshot, recording, terminal capture, console output, redacted runtime log, linked artifact, or copied live output):

```text

  "url": "https://connect.composio.dev/mcp",

}
```

- What was not tested: a full replacement of my production gateway package with this branch as the long-running service. The focused real proof used a branch build/projection check plus live Codex/remote-MCP protocol calls.
- Proof limitations or environment constraints: Composio-specific account/app availability depends on the authenticated user's Composio workspace. The proof verifies OAuth projection and MCP protocol authentication, not every downstream Composio app integration.
- Before evidence (optional but encouraged): before this change, the OpenClaw schema/types/projection path had no way to represent or emit `oauth_resource` / `oauth.client_id` from `mcp.servers` into Codex MCP config.

## Tests and validation

Which commands did you run?

```text
pnpm install
pnpm exec vitest run extensions/codex/src/app-server/thread-lifecycle.user-mcp-servers.test.ts src/agents/codex-mcp-config.test.ts src/agents/cli-runner/bundle-mcp-codex.user-config.test.ts src/agents/cli-runner/bundle-mcp.codex.test.ts src/config/schema.test.ts src/config/schema.base.generated.test.ts src/config/config-misc.test.ts
```

target.title: fix(gmail-watcher): catch renewal interval errors
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Gmail watcher sets up a `setInterval` that calls `startGmailWatch(runtimeConfig)` as a fire-and-forget `void` expression in two places:

1. The gateway watcher (`src/hooks/gmail-watcher.ts`).
2. The foreground `openclaw webhooks gmail run` path (`src/hooks/gmail-ops.ts`).

In the foreground path, the local `startGmailWatch` helper does **not** internally catch `runCommandWithTimeout` failures. If the periodic Gmail API watch registration rejects, the rejection becomes an unhandled rejection and can crash the foreground process hours after startup.

## Why This Change Was Made

Added a `.catch` to both renewal `startGmailWatch` calls. On rejection, a warning/error is logged and the watcher keeps running, so the next renewal cycle can retry. The initial startup path is unchanged.

## User Impact

Long-running gateway and foreground Gmail watchers no longer crash on transient Gmail API renewal failures.

## Evidence

Real behavior proof builds fake `gog` executables on disk, prepends them to `PATH`, and exercises the actual watcher code. The fake `gog` succeeds on the initial `watch start`, runs `serve`, then deletes itself so every subsequent renewal `watch start` fails with `ENOENT`.

```bash

```

After the fix both paths pass:
