target.title: fix #95295: [Bug]: Web UI sidebar hides existing child-spawned subagent sessions across agent scopes
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: The Web UI sidebar Recent Sessions list could hide existing child-spawned subagent transcripts when the current chat scope was another agent, so users could not intentionally rediscover those sessions from the left sidebar.
- Solution: Keep the default scoped sidebar behavior, but add an explicit sidebar **All agents** mode for sidebar-owned Recent Sessions refresh/search/display only.
- What changed: Migrated the original fix onto the current Control UI architecture (`AppSidebar`, `SessionPicker`, `SessionCapability`, `SessionsPage`, and session navigation helpers). Sidebar-owned all-agents requests omit `agentId` and include child/spawned subagent rows; default scoped mode still filters by the active chat agent and hides child/spawned subagent rows. Checkpoint opener, checkpoint branch/restore, and chat-send refreshes remain scoped to their target session/agent.
- What did NOT change / out of scope: This does not change gateway protocol/schema, stored transcript format, migration behavior, public config, the default scoped sidebar view, or make **All agents** a global Sessions-tab mode.
- Why it matters / User impact: Users with persisted child-spawned subagent work can intentionally find and reopen those existing transcripts from the sidebar without losing the safer default scoped view, and non-sidebar refreshes do not accidentally broaden to all agents.
- Fixes #95295

## What Problem This Solves

The sidebar needed an intentional way to rediscover persisted child-spawned subagent sessions across agent scopes. The conflict resolution also had to preserve the follow-up boundary repairs from the existing PR: sidebar **All agents** must stay local to the sidebar, while checkpoint entry, checkpoint mutation, and chat-send refreshes must keep using the current/checkpoint/target session's agent scope.

## Root Cause

- **Root cause:** Recent Sessions had a request/filter invariant mismatch: the sidebar requested the current agent's session list and then filtered out child/subagent-spawned rows, which made persisted child-spawned sessions from another agent scope undiscoverable from the sidebar.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** The fix makes the request/filter invariant explicit. Default sidebar mode still requests and filters scoped rows. The new sidebar-owned **All agents** mode intentionally requests without `agentId` and opts the sidebar visibility helper into child/spawned rows. Non-sidebar refreshes derive scope from the current/checkpoint/target session key instead of reading sidebar state, so the all-agents opt-in cannot leak into checkpoint, Sessions-page, or chat-send refreshes.
- **Fix classification:** Root-cause UI/session-state fix with bounded conflict-resolution migration to the current Control UI architecture.
- **Maintainer-ready confidence:** High for the scoped code/test repair after the rebase conflict migration; maintainer product selection remains required because sibling candidate PRs (#95304 and #95307) exist with different scopes.
- **Patch quality notes:** The two `as unknown as ...` casts are confined to Vitest mocks that adapt a minimal fake client/host to existing test-only interfaces; production code does not add type escapes. The `return undefined` branch in `SessionsPage.sessionListAgentId` is a no-context guard for a helper that cannot compute scope without application context; callers already treat missing `agentId` as an unscoped list option. The diff is slightly over the file-count preference because the old `ui/src/ui/...` implementation was deleted on main and the same behavior had to be migrated into the new component/capability/page layout rather than restoring deleted files.
- **Architecture / source-of-truth check:** The source of truth remains the existing `sessions.list` request contract and session keys (`agent:<agentId>:...`). Sidebar Recent Sessions owns the **All agents** opt-in request/filter behavior; checkpoint and chat flows own their target-session scope. No protocol, schema, storage, migration, transcript format, gateway contract, or public config is changed.

## Implementation Notes

- `ui/src/lib/sessions/navigation.ts` now accepts a sidebar all-agents flag. Default navigation stays scoped and hides child/spawned subagent rows; all-agents mode disables agent filtering for the sidebar list and includes child/spawned rows while preserving archived/global/unknown/cron exclusions.
- `ui/src/components/app-sidebar.ts` owns the **All agents** toggle and uses it only for sidebar Recent Sessions refresh/navigation/picker state.
- `ui/src/components/session-picker.ts` omits `agentId` only when the explicit all-agents picker mode is active; default picker rows remain filtered to the current agent.
- `ui/src/lib/sessions/index.ts` derives checkpoint branch/restore refresh scope from the checkpoint session key or explicit agent override, so checkpoint mutations do not inherit a shared all-agents list state.
- `ui/src/pages/sessions/sessions-page.ts` scopes checkpoint-opener list loads to the checkpoint session's agent.
- `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-send.test.ts`, `ui/src/lib/sessions/index.test.ts`, and `ui/src/lib/sessions/navigation.test.ts` lock in the scoped/non-scoped boundaries.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Default sidebar Recent Sessions remains scoped to the active chat agent and excludes child/spawned subagent sessions. Pressing **All agents** on the sidebar intentionally allows cross-agent child/spawned subagent sessions to appear there. Checkpoint opener, checkpoint branch/restore, and chat-send `sessions.list` refreshes remain scoped to the current/checkpoint/target session's agent and do not inherit the sidebar all-agents toggle.
- **Real environment tested:** Local OpenClaw PR worktree on Windows/Git Bash, with pnpm workspace dependencies installed. The environment has Node `v22.17.0` and pnpm `11.2.2`; pnpm emitted the repo's non-fatal engine warning requesting Node `>=22.19.0 <23 || >=23.11.0`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** `git diff --check`; `pnpm check:no-conflict-markers`; `pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 ui/src/components/app-sidebar.ts ui/src/components/session-picker.ts ui/src/lib/sessions/index.test.ts ui/src/lib/sessions/index.ts ui/src/lib/sessions/navigation.test.ts ui/src/lib/sessions/navigation.ts ui/src/pages/chat/chat-send.test.ts ui/src/pages/sessions/sessions-page.ts ui/src/styles/layout.css`; `pnpm --dir ui test src/lib/sessions/navigation.test.ts src/lib/sessions/index.test.ts src/pages/chat/chat-send.test.ts`; `pnpm check:test-types`; `pnpm lint`.
- **Evidence after fix:** `git diff --check` and `pnpm check:no-conflict-markers` exited 0. The scoped formatter check exited 0 for all 9 changed files. The focused UI/session regression command exited 0 with 3 test files and 104 tests passing. `pnpm check:test-types` exited 0. `pnpm lint` exited 0.
- **Observed result after fix:** The navigation tests assert default scoped rows stay on the active agent and hide child/spawned subagent rows, while explicit sidebar all-agents mode includes a cross-agent spawned/subagent row and still filters cron rows. The session capability test asserts checkpoint branch/restore for `agent:review:*` refresh `sessions.list` with `agentId: "review"`. The chat send test asserts post-send refresh for `agent:ops:*` uses `agentId: "ops"`.
- **What was not tested:** I could not run a long-lived live gateway/Mantis/private transcript proof in this contributor environment, so this PR does not claim real Mantis or private live-gateway coverage. `pnpm check:changed` could not run because local `crabbox` failed its basic sanity check before delegating to Blacksmith Testbox. Full `pnpm --dir ui test` was attempted but is not usable as local proof here because unrelated baseline tests failed under the Chinese system locale and Vitest browser tests could not launch without an installed Playwright Chromium binary; the focused changed-file UI/session regressions above passed.

## Review findings addressed

- Current refreshed review checklist has no actionable line-review findings.
- The previous old-architecture `ui/src/ui/...` implementation conflicts were not restored. Their behavior was migrated into the current Control UI architecture files listed above.
- PR #95320 still has sibling candidate PR references (#95304 and #95307) in the linked issue context. This PR intentionally stays on the narrow same-contract UI path; final product/canonical selection remains a maintainer decision.

## Regression Test Plan

- **Target test file:** `ui/src/lib/sessions/navigation.test.ts`, `ui/src/lib/sessions/index.test.ts`, and `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-send.test.ts`.
- **Target test files:** `ui/src/lib/sessions/navigation.test.ts`, `ui/src/lib/sessions/index.test.ts`, and `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-send.test.ts`.
- **Scenario locked in:** Explicit sidebar all-agents mode is the only path that both omits sidebar request `agentId` and includes child/spawned subagent rows. Default sidebar mode remains scoped to the active chat agent. Checkpoint opener and checkpoint branch/restore refreshes stay scoped to the checkpoint/current session agent. Post-send refreshes stay scoped to the target chat session agent.
- **Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail:** The navigation tests guard the sidebar request/filter boundary, the session capability test guards checkpoint mutation refresh scope, and the chat-send test guards shared post-send refresh scope. Together they prevent the sidebar toggle from becoming a global session-list mode without requiring gateway/protocol/storage changes.

## Merge risk

- **Risk labels considered:** session-state / security-boundary / compatibility / UI visibility.
- **Risk explanation:** The diff touches session-state UI filtering and a scope control, which can affect whether existing child-spawned transcripts are visible in the sidebar. Compatibility risk is limited because explicit/default scoped refreshes remain authoritative outside the sidebar and no public protocol, schema, config, storage format, transcript format, or migration contract changes.
- **Why acceptable:** The new cross-agent visibility is default-off, explicitly user-selected, and limited to the sidebar Recent Sessions list. Existing archived/global/unknown/cron exclusions remain. Checkpoint and chat refreshes stay scoped, so enabling **All agents** does not widen non-sidebar refreshes.

target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a sibling OOM gap in OpenAI Codex OAuth image generation. The Codex Responses SSE path already bounds streamed bodies in `readResponseBodyText`, but the `!response.body` branch still called `response.text()` and only checked `MAX_CODEX_IMAGE_SSE_BYTES` after buffering the full payload. A faulty or hostile endpoint returning a body without a readable stream could still grow gateway memory without bound before the size guard fired.

## Why This Change Was Made

The no-body branch now fail-closes before any full-buffer fallback:

- reject oversized bodies from a trustworthy `Content-Length` header before calling `readResponseWithLimit` / `arrayBuffer()`
- reject missing or invalid `Content-Length` when no readable stream exists, instead of reading an unknown-size body
- only read bounded no-body payloads when `Content-Length` is present and within `MAX_CODEX_IMAGE_SSE_BYTES` (64 MiB)

This follows the same invariant as the existing streamed Codex image SSE guard:

- streamed Codex image SSE responses remain incrementally capped and cancelled on overflow
- no-body Codex image responses now reject early from `Content-Length` or fail closed when length is unknown
- loopback transport proof exercises the production Codex OAuth image path over real HTTP on `127.0.0.1`

## User Impact

Operators using Codex OAuth image generation through the Responses transport are protected when a provider returns an oversized or unknown-size payload on the no-body response path. Valid Codex image SSE responses continue to work unchanged.

## Evidence

Loopback transport proof: I ran the production Codex OAuth `generateImage` path against a local HTTP server on `127.0.0.1`. This uses the real `postJsonRequest` / `fetchWithSsrFGuard` path, real HTTP `Response` streams/headers, OAuth auth stubbing only, and no mocked `postJsonRequest`.

    "ok": true,
    "images": 1,
    "cancelObserved": false,
    "payloadBytes": 277,
    "ms": 1490
  },
  "oversizedStream": {
    "mode": "oversized-stream-cancel-over-loopback",
    "ok": true,
    "error": "OpenAI Codex image generation response exceeded size limit",
    "cancelObserved": true,
    "payloadBytes": 70254592,
    "ms": 819
  },
  "oversizedNoBody": {
    "mode": "oversized-no-body-over-loopback",
    "ok": true,
    "error": "OpenAI Codex image generation response exceeded size limit",
    "bodyNullSimulated": true,
    "earlyReject": true,
    "arrayBufferCalled": false,
    "contentLengthBytes": 67108865,
    "payloadBytes": 67108865,
    "ms": 148
  }

```

- Unknown-size no-body responses fail closed with `OpenAI Codex image generation response missing readable body stream`.

## 2026-06-28 rescue update

- Rebased the contributor branch onto current `origin/main` (`830467bc93`) and resolved the only manual conflict in `ui/src/lib/chat/message-extract.ts`, preserving both main's `isTextContentBlockType(...)` support and this PR's trusted bare-body extraction path.

Added a regression test covering `{ ...message, content: "[redacted]" }`.
- Fixed the current ClawSweeper P1 type blocker: `resolveTrustedInboundBareBody(...)` now accepts any message-like object (`object | null | undefined`) and defensively reads the runtime-attached trusted fields, which removes the `TS2559` failures at the LLM-boundary and CLI imported-history call sites without requiring unsafe call-site casts. (An earlier attempt used a generic `<T extends object>`; that tripped `no-unnecessary-type-parameters` in `check-lint`, so the parameter is a plain `object`.)
- Kept memory-host session-file tests stable on Windows by asserting classification paths through the exported comparison normalizer and tolerating transient `EBUSY`/`ENOTEMPTY`/`EPERM` fixture cleanup during teardown. No cross-package import is added, so the memory-host-sdk private-package contract surface is unchanged (the `checks-fast-contracts-plugins-b` boundary check passes).
- Resolved the merge conflict: PR head is now `MERGEABLE` against `main`.

Local note: direct extension type-check targets were also attempted, but the local shared `node_modules` symlink is missing unrelated extension dependencies/exports (`@openclaw/crabline`, `acpx/runtime` members) in files outside this PR's diff; core production/test type-check targets for the touched code pass as shown above.

## Summary

- **What did NOT change:** This does not remove legacy sentinel stripping for already-persisted rows, does not migrate transcript files, does not change active-turn model prompt construction, and does not add unrelated provider/channel routing behavior.
- **Why it matters / User impact:** Users who paste or type literal metadata-looking text should not lose that text from the control UI, CLI imported-session dedupe, memory session corpus, or model historical replay when OpenClaw has a trusted bare body for the inbound turn.
- Behavior or issue addressed: user-authored text that looks like OpenClaw inbound metadata could be stripped or deduped incorrectly because consumers parsed forgeable sentinel text from `content`.

## Real behavior proof

- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/cli-session-history.test.ts src/auto-reply/inbound.test.ts src/sessions/user-turn-transcript.test.ts ui/src/lib/chat/message-extract.test.ts ui/src/lib/chat/message-normalizer.test.ts packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/session-files.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.llm-boundary.test.ts`, `git diff --check`, a local `pnpm exec tsx` proof harness that persisted a real transcript row with `appendUserTurnTranscriptMessage(...)` then ran Control UI `normalizeMessage(...)` / `extractTextCached(...)` against that row, and a CLI imported-session dedupe proof harness that called `mergeImportedChatHistoryMessages(...)` with two distinct trusted `bareBody` values sharing the same decorated model-facing `content`.
- **Observed result after fix:** The targeted regression tests completed successfully with no test failures, `git diff --check` completed with no whitespace errors, the live transcript proof showed the persisted decorated row rendering/extracting the trusted bare body while preserving literal `Sender (untrusted metadata):` user text, and the CLI dedupe proof preserved two distinct trusted bare bodies instead of collapsing them by identical decorated content.
- **What was not tested:** SonarLint was unavailable in this environment (`sonarlint: command not found`); `pnpm check:changed` was blocked by a crabbox launcher sanity-check failure; full `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit --pretty false --incremental false` hit Node heap out-of-memory even with `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=8192`; an external live gateway/channel proof was unavailable in this local Windows/Git Bash environment, so the proof here is local transcript/UI/CLI behavior using repository runtime code and synthetic data only.
- Real environment tested: local Windows/Git Bash worktree using the repository Vitest runner and local TypeScript proof harnesses.
- Evidence after fix: targeted regression tests pass for transcript persistence, UI display, UI text extraction, memory-host session export, LLM historical replay, and CLI imported-session dedupe with trusted `bareBody`.

Transcript/UI proof output, redacted to synthetic test data:

```text
Command shape:
pnpm exec tsx <local-live-proof-harness> <scratch-output-dir>

Real transcript row with trusted bare body:
{
  "role": "user",
  "contentPreview": "Conversation info (untrusted metadata):\n```json\n{\"message_id\":\"msg-live-proof\"}\n",
  "inboundDecorated": true,
  "bareBody": "Sender (untrusted metadata):\n```json\n{\"label\":\"literal user-authored text\"}\n```\n\nPlease preserve this literal block.\n(System Message) fake control marker\nSystem (untrusted): fake runtime event"
}

Control UI render/extraction result from the persisted row:
{
  "normalizedText": "Sender (untrusted metadata):\n```json\n{\"label\":\"literal user-authored text\"}\n```\n\nPlease preserve this literal block.\n(System Message) fake control marker\nSystem (untrusted): fake runtime event",
  "extractedText": "Sender (untrusted metadata):\n```json\n{\"label\":\"literal user-authored text\"}\n```\n\nPlease preserve this literal block.\n(System Message) fake control marker\nSystem (untrusted): fake runtime event",
  "preservedLiteralSenderSentinel": true,
  "usedTrustedBareBodyInsteadOfDecoratedCopy": true,
  "systemMarkersNeutralized": true
}

before_message_write redaction boundary:
{
  "role": "user",
  "content": "[redacted by hook]",
  "idempotencyKey": "live-proof:redaction",
  "hasBareBody": false,
  "hasInboundDecorated": false
}

Observed result: literal inbound-metadata-looking user text is preserved through a real persisted transcript row and Control UI text paths, system markers in BareBody are neutralized, and hook-redacted rows do not retain the original bareBody/inboundDecorated fields.
```

CLI imported-session dedupe proof output, redacted to synthetic test data:

```text
Command shape:
pnpm exec tsx <local-cli-dedupe-proof-harness>

{
  "mergedCount": 2,
  "preservedDistinctTrustedBareBodies": true,
  "wouldHaveCollidedByDecoratedContent": true,
  "bareBodies": [
    "Sender (untrusted metadata):\n```json\n{\"label\":\"literal first user text\"}\n```\n\nPlease preserve first",
    "Sender (untrusted metadata):\n```json\n{\"label\":\"literal second user text\"}\n```\n\nPlease preserve second"
  ]
}

Observed result: the CLI merge path kept both rows because trusted bare bodies differ, even though both rows had the same decorated model-facing content and would have collided if dedupe still used only forgeable sentinel-stripped content.
```

## Regression Test Plan

- **Target test file:** `src/gateway/cli-session-history.test.ts`, `src/auto-reply/inbound.test.ts`, `src/sessions/user-turn-transcript.test.ts`, `ui/src/lib/chat/message-extract.test.ts`, `ui/src/lib/chat/message-normalizer.test.ts`, `packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/session-files.test.ts`, and `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.llm-boundary.test.ts`.
- **Scenario locked in:** Each consumer test covers a decorated inbound turn whose trusted bare body contains sentinel-shaped user text such as `Sender (untrusted metadata):` plus fenced JSON; the expected behavior is that the trusted bare body is preserved literally instead of being parsed and stripped as metadata. The CLI imported-session test additionally proves two messages with identical decorated `content` but different trusted `bareBody` values do not dedupe into one row.
- **Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail:** It locks the shared trusted-contract behavior at the persistence, UI, CLI dedupe, memory, and LLM replay boundaries without removing the legacy sentinel fallback or asserting unrelated prompt-construction details.

## Root Cause

- **Root cause:** The parser/contract boundary was wrong: `buildInboundUserContextPrefix(...)` creates inbound metadata as plaintext blocks for model-facing prompts, and consumers such as UI history normalization, CLI imported-session dedupe, memory-host session export, and LLM historical replay had no trusted way to distinguish host-added decoration from user-authored text in the same `content` channel.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** The source-of-truth decision is no longer derived from forgeable `content` text. Consumers now use the shared trusted resolver and only accept `bareBody` when the message/context is explicitly marked `inboundDecorated: true` / `InboundDecorated: true`, so sentinel parsing remains only a legacy compatibility path.
- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix for a public/data-format contract bug.
- **Maintainer-ready confidence:** High. The change is additive, keeps legacy fallback behavior, and has targeted regression coverage for the affected consumer paths.
- **Patch quality notes:** Dynamic `as unknown` casts stay at existing message-union boundaries where `AgentMessage` can carry additive metadata; guard/default returns preserve existing fallback behavior; the multi-file diff follows the shared consumer contract boundary and is not a downstream masking workaround.
- **Architecture / source-of-truth check:** The canonical contract is the inbound user-turn/message metadata (`inboundDecorated` plus `bareBody`, mirrored as `InboundDecorated` plus `BareBody` on inbound context). Display/history/CLI dedupe/memory consumers use that trusted contract when present and only parse text sentinels for unmarked legacy content.

## What Problem This Solves

Inbound context decoration is host-generated, but the decorated copy can live as text inside user-controlled user message content. Several consumers stripped or compared that decoration by matching forgeable sentinel strings such as `Sender (untrusted metadata):` and fenced JSON. If a user typed the same shape intentionally, downstream display/history/dedupe/memory paths could drop real user text or collapse distinct imported messages.

This PR gives consumers a trusted, out-of-band contract for decorated inbound turns: a message/context marker that says the content may be decorated, plus the host-authored bare body to render/replay/index/dedupe.

## Source-of-truth boundary

The canonical contract is the inbound user-turn/message metadata:

- runtime/persisted user messages: `inboundDecorated: true` plus `bareBody`
- inbound context: `InboundDecorated` plus `BareBody`

The model-facing prompt may still carry inbound context for the active turn. Display/history/CLI dedupe/memory consumers should use the trusted bare body when present, and only parse text sentinels for unmarked legacy content.

## Implementation summary

- Add optional trusted inbound fields:
  - `inboundDecorated: true` / `bareBody` on persisted/runtime user messages.
  - `InboundDecorated` / `BareBody` on inbound template context.
- Persist the trusted bare body on decorated user turns, while respecting `before_message_write` hooks as the redaction boundary: if a hook replaces content without returning trusted fields, the original `bareBody` / `inboundDecorated` is dropped.
- Update UI display, UI text extraction/export/search, CLI imported-session dedupe, memory-host session indexing, and LLM historical replay to prefer the trusted bare body before falling back to legacy sentinel stripping.
- Keep existing `stripInboundMetadata(...)` behavior for old transcripts that do not carry the trusted fields.

## Scope boundary

In scope: contract/type plumbing for inbound user turns, transcript persistence/runtime merge preservation, UI display normalization, CLI imported-session dedupe, memory-host session export/indexing, LLM historical replay normalization, and regression tests for those paths.

Out of scope: removing legacy sentinel stripping for already-persisted rows, changing active-turn model prompt construction, migrating existing transcript files, or doing a broad plugin SDK redesign beyond optional trusted fields.

## Related PR scan

The daily-fix related open PR scan found related PR #94419 as advisory background only. This PR does not depend on that work and keeps the fix scoped to the trusted inbound bare-body contract requested by #95279.

## Review findings addressed

- RF-001 / RF-004 / RF-007 / RF-008 — fixed in `src/gateway/cli-session-history.merge.ts`: the CLI imported-session comparable-text path now calls `resolveTrustedInboundBareBody(...)` for trusted decorated user messages before falling back to legacy sentinel stripping. Regression coverage: `src/gateway/cli-session-history.test.ts` verifies two imported/local user turns with identical decorated content but distinct sentinel-shaped trusted bare bodies remain two messages.
- RF-002 / RF-003 — addressed with redacted terminal proof for the CLI imported-session dedupe path. The proof called `mergeImportedChatHistoryMessages(...)` with two trusted bare bodies and identical decorated content; output showed `mergedCount: 2`, `preservedDistinctTrustedBareBodies: true`, and `wouldHaveCollidedByDecoratedContent: true`.
- RF-005 / RF-006 — addressed by keeping the durable contract explicit and additive: `inboundDecorated` gates trust in `bareBody`, consumers use the shared resolver, legacy unmarked rows keep sentinel fallback behavior, and `before_message_write` remains the redaction boundary by dropping original trusted fields when hooks replace content without returning trusted fields themselves.
- RF-009 — passed: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/cli-session-history.test.ts` completed successfully with no test failures.
- RF-010 — passed: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/inbound.test.ts src/sessions/user-turn-transcript.test.ts ui/src/lib/chat/message-extract.test.ts ui/src/lib/chat/message-normalizer.test.ts packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/session-files.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.llm-boundary.test.ts` completed successfully with no test failures, and the same run was repeated including `src/gateway/cli-session-history.test.ts` after the CLI dedupe fix was committed.
- RF-011 — passed: `git diff --check` completed with exit code 0 and no whitespace errors.
- Previous ClawSweeper P1 (`before_message_write` redaction boundary) — fixed in `src/sessions/user-turn-transcript.ts`: `preparePersistedUserTurnMessageForTranscriptWrite(...)` now detects when a `before_message_write` hook rewrites the message `content` (the common `{ ...message, content: "[redacted]" }` spread pattern). When the hook's returned `content` differs from the incoming `content`, the persisted turn drops the original trusted `bareBody` and `inboundDecorated`, so downstream UI/replay/memory consumers can no longer trust text the hook meant to redact; idempotency keys are still preserved. Regression coverage: `src/sessions/user-turn-transcript.test.ts` adds a case where a redaction hook returns `{ ...message, content: "[redacted by hook]" }` against a decorated secret prompt and asserts the persisted row has neither `bareBody` nor `inboundDecorated`.
- Previous ClawSweeper P1 (`BareBody` sanitizer) — fixed in `src/auto-reply/reply/inbound-context.ts`: `BareBody` now uses the same inbound system-marker neutralization path as `RawBody` / `CommandBody` instead of newline-only trusted normalization. Regression coverage: `src/auto-reply/inbound.test.ts` asserts `[System Message]` and line-leading `System:` markers are neutralized on `BareBody`.
- Previous ClawSweeper UI extraction finding — fixed in `ui/src/lib/chat/message-extract.ts`: `extractText(...)` / `extractTextCached(...)` now use the shared `resolveTrustedInboundBareBody(...)` path for trusted decorated user messages before legacy sentinel stripping. Regression coverage: `ui/src/lib/chat/message-extract.test.ts` verifies sentinel-shaped user-authored text is preserved for export/search/text-extraction consumers.

## Verification

Passed locally (local Windows/Git Bash worktree, repository Vitest + tsgo runners):

```

node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core-test.tsbuildinfo   # exit 0

```

Targeted regression results after this update:

- `src/sessions/user-turn-transcript.test.ts` — 28 passed, including the new "drops trusted bare body when before_message_write spreads and rewrites content" case.
- `src/gateway/cli-session-history.test.ts` — 60 passed.
- `src/auto-reply/inbound.test.ts` — 61 passed.
- `ui/src/lib/chat/message-extract.test.ts` — 11 passed.
- `ui/src/lib/chat/message-normalizer.test.ts` — 34 passed.
- `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.llm-boundary.test.ts` — passed.
- `packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/session-files.test.ts` — 38 passed. This file initially failed 3 `listSessionTranscriptCorpusEntriesForAgent` cases on Windows (`EBUSY` sqlite unlink + `C:\Windows\TEMP` vs `c:\windows\temp` path-case mismatch); the same 3 failed identically on a clean `origin/main` checkout. Closes #100162

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where cron-driven embedded agent runs could appear completed even when the final assistant turn produced no deliverable reply, leaving the configured channel without a response or failure signal.

## Why This Change Was Made

Cron finalization now treats a delivery-requested embedded run with no final payload or synthesized text as a cron run error instead of passing it into the silent delivery path. The guard preserves intentional silent replies, message-tool/source deliveries that already satisfied the target, and committed terminal progress such as deterministic approval prompts, accepted child sessions, or successful cron adds, so this does not change explicit no-reply, already-delivered, approval-pending, or handoff-only flows.

## User Impact

Operators and channel users now get an observable cron failure state for empty final assistant completions instead of a dark lane where the job is marked complete but no reply reaches the destination.

## Evidence

- Added focused regressions for a completed embedded run with delivery requested and no final payload. They assert the plain empty completion and unverified/off-target message-tool attempts become `error` with no dispatch, while deterministic approval prompts, accepted child-session handoffs, and successful cron-add completions are not misclassified as cron errors.
- Focused regression passed: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.cron.config.ts src/cron/isolated-agent/run.meta-error-status.test.ts` (10 tests).

The proof forced a delivery-requested isolated cron run whose mock model exhausted into an empty visible response; the run log showed `status=error`, `delivery=not-delivered`, and the qa-channel received one failure notification instead of the normal `EMPTY-EXHAUSTED-OK` success reply.
- Live cron proof passed using qa-lab with qa-channel, a real gateway child process, and live-frontier `claude-cli/opus`. The run stored a one-minute cron reminder, forced execution, completed via the cron path, and observed the QA channel delivery marker `QA-CRON-5df256c5`.

target.title: fix(update-check): wrap malformed npm view JSON parse in try/catch
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`fetchNpmPackageTargetStatus` bounds `npm view --json` stdout to 1 MiB, but when the bounded string is malformed JSON the parse failure currently surfaces as a raw `SyntaxError` string through the outer catch. That gives callers no indication the failure came from npm metadata parsing.

## Why This Change Was Made

Wrapped `JSON.parse` inside `parseNpmPackageTargetMetadata` with a contextual `try/catch`. The error is rethrown with the parse cause and is then caught by the existing `fetchNpmPackageTargetStatus` catch block, so the function returns `{ version: null, nodeEngine: null, error: ... }` with a clear "npm view returned invalid JSON" message.

## User Impact

Update/status checks report clearer diagnostics when npm returns malformed metadata; it is easier to distinguish an npm-side JSON glitch from other command failures.

## Evidence

Terminal proof (after fix) uses a real fake `npm` executable on disk:

target.title: fix(ios): restore in-flight runs after reconnect
target.body:
Part of #100197. Supersedes the stacked `afterSeq` design in #100267.

## What Problem This Solves

When iOS backgrounds, reconnects, changes sessions, or misses an event sequence, it can lose ownership of a run that is still active on the Gateway. The transcript may look idle, Abort disappears, and a second send becomes possible while the first run is still working.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway already exposes the canonical active-run snapshot through `chat.history.inFlightRun`; the TUI already consumes that contract. This rewrite removes every proposed `afterSeq` protocol/client change and restores ownership from the existing snapshot instead.

The shared Apple chat model now:

- adopts active run ID and buffered text during bootstrap, foreground resume, sequence-gap recovery, immediate post-send refresh, delayed retries, and completion refreshes;
- orders history snapshots against newer live deltas, terminal events, session messages, session switches, agent changes, and concurrent history requests;
- keeps ownership stable when another client streams a different run in the same session;
- scopes bare-global/default-agent aliases and non-default agent-qualified global sessions without cross-agent transcript adoption;
- distinguishes current Gateway negative state via `sessionInfo.hasActiveRun` from legacy gateways that omit active-run metadata;
- preserves live/provisional transcript rows when delayed history arrives, including identical replies from different turns;
- rearms timeouts safely and clears silent completed/failed runs from authoritative current-Gateway state.

Codex app-server source confirms a turn becomes `InProgress` with no message items before later `AgentMessageDelta` notifications (`codex-rs/app-server/src/bespoke_event_handling.rs:155`, `codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/event_mapping.rs:359`). That is why an active run with an empty buffered string is still valid ownership.

## User Impact

Returning to iOS or macOS chat no longer loses an active response. Streaming text, tool state, Abort, and the send lock recover without adding a Gateway protocol or cursor, while older Gateways retain the prior transcript-based completion fallback.

## Evidence

- `swift test --package-path apps/shared/OpenClawKit --filter ChatViewModelTests` — 129/129 passed after rebase, including unrelated session activity without a chat-run snapshot.
- `swift build --package-path apps/macos` — passed after rebase.
- SwiftFormat lint with `config/swiftformat` — clean for every touched Swift file.
- Final full-branch Codex autoreview — clean; no accepted/actionable findings after separating session-wide activity from chat-run ownership.
- Direct Gateway contract review: `src/gateway/server-methods/chat.ts`, `src/gateway/server-session-events.ts`, and `src/gateway/server-methods/session-active-runs.ts`.
- Direct Codex contract review at `be33f80bc65159c094ecd06bf155afa3061ce23d`: `codex-rs/app-server/src/bespoke_event_handling.rs:155-183`, `codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/event_mapping.rs:359-367`, and `codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/turn.rs:375-378`.

Visual reconnect/background proof is requested separately on this exact head.

target.title: fix: WebChat stop fails for WeChat channel sessions
target.body:
Related: #91987

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes WebChat `/stop` failing to stop looping channel-originated agent turns, observed with a WeChat channel session selected in WebChat.

## Why This Change Was Made

WebChat exact stop text now bypasses slash-menu selection and is submitted as the typed command, so `/stop` reliably reaches the abort path.

The gateway abort path now preserves the selected explicit channel session key across the active state used by this flow:

- `chatAbortControllers` for normal WebChat/chat runs
- hidden registered or pre-registered channel runs when the request names that explicit channel session
- `replyRunRegistry` for active channel auto-reply operations that do not have a chat abort controller

Broad `agent:main`/global stop requests no longer infer a hidden channel session. They abort only matching visible/global scope unless the request already carries the explicit channel session key.

## User Impact

Users viewing a WeChat/channel session in WebChat can stop a looping channel agent with `/stop`. Broad visible sessions still do not accidentally stop unrelated hidden channel work.

target.title: fix(ui): preserve live tool stream order
target.body: ## What Problem This Solves Live WebChat tool cards were reordered incorrectly when a tool event timestamp was older than the assistant stream segment that introduced that tool call. The timestamp-only sorter could place tool cards *before* their causal assistant text. ## Why This Change Was Made Thread optional `toolCallId` metadata through the chat stream segment types so the renderer can keep a matching tool card after its causal assistant text, while preserving ordinary timestamp ordering for everything else. `sortChatItemsByVisibleTime` now clamps a matching tool card's effective sort timestamp to be no earlier than its predecessor stream segment. Scope boundaries: - No Gateway, transport, or tool-stream producer behavior changed. The real WebChat path already writes `{ text, ts, toolCallId }` into `chatStreamSegments` in `ui/src/ui/app-tool-stream.ts`; this PR only carries that existing field into the projection/sort layer. - Ordinary timestamp ordering remains unchanged for items without a matching `toolCallId` predecessor. - Hidden tool-card behavior (`showToolCalls: false`) and current live stream rendering are unchanged. ## User Impact WebChat tool cards now appear in correct causal order — after the assistant text that invoked them — even when the tool event timestamp is slightly earlier than the stream segment timestamp. No behavior change for normal correctly ordered timestamps. ## Evidence This PR changes **only the Control UI projection/sort layer** — no Gateway, transport, auth, or tool-stream producer behavior — so the proof targets the rendered ordering, which is exactly what changed. All four proofs below were **re-run on PR head `8d7d85f15cba` (Node v22.22.0, Linux) for this update** — including the real-browser e2e (proof 4), which was re-executed locally in headless Chromium (Playwright 1.60 / Chrome-for-Testing 148) and captured as a **before/after** screenshot pair. ### 1. Production projection output — real `buildChatItems` (re-verified) Driving the real `buildChatItems` with the inversion scenario (tool ts `1000` older than the introducing stream segment ts `2000`): ```bash node --import tsx --no-warnings <<'NODE' import { buildChatItems } from './ui/src/ui/chat/build-chat-items.ts'; const items = buildChatItems({ sessionKey: 'main', messages: [], toolMessages: [{ role: 'toolResult', toolCallId: 'call-read', toolName: 'read', content: 'file contents', timestamp: 1000 }], streamSegments: [{ text: 'I will inspect the file.', ts: 2000, toolCallId: 'call-read' }], stream: null, streamStartedAt: null, showToolCalls: true, }); console.log(items.map((i) => ('kind' in i && i.kind === 'stream') ? `stream:${i.text}` : `tool:${i.messages?.[0]?.message?.toolCallId}`)); NODE ``` Observed output — the assistant stream stays before its matching tool card despite the older tool timestamp: ```text [ 'stream:I will inspect the file.', 'tool:call-read' ] ``` ### 2. Regression with fix (re-verified) ```text $ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/ui/chat/build-chat-items.test.ts Test Files 1 passed (1) / Tests 45 passed (45) ``` ### 3. Negative control (re-verified) Reverting only `ui/src/ui/chat/build-chat-items.ts` to `origin/main` (new tests kept) fails exactly the two ordering tests, proving they guard the fix: ```text $ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/ui/chat/build-chat-items.test.ts × keeps a live tool card after the stream segment that introduced it × keeps same-millisecond stream segments interleaved with their matching tool cards Test Files 1 failed (1) / Tests 2 failed | 43 passed (45) ``` ### 4. Real-browser e2e — re-run locally in real Chromium, before/after screenshots `ui/src/ui/e2e/chat-flow.e2e.test.ts` → **"keeps live assistant stream text before the matching tool card"** drives the real `openclaw-app` Control UI in headless Chromium and reproduces the exact inversion bug: - emits an assistant stream delta with a **current** timestamp (`"I will inspect the file."`); - emits the matching `read` tool event with an **older** timestamp (`ts: Date.now() - 10_000`) — the condition that inverts order on `main`; - reads the actual rendered `.chat-thread` DOM and asserts `expect(visibleOrder).toEqual(["assistant stream", "tool card"])`. Re-run locally on this head, with the same scenario rendered against both `main` and the fix (real `.chat-thread` DOM order read from the live UI): ```text # WITH FIX (head 8d7d85f) $ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts \ --configLoader runner ui/src/ui/e2e/chat-flow.e2e.test.ts \ -t "keeps live assistant stream text before the matching tool card" Test Files 1 passed (1) / Tests 1 passed | 16 skipped (17) rendered .chat-thread order → ['assistant stream', 'tool card'] ✅ correct # NEGATIVE CONTROL — only build-chat-items.ts reverted to origin/main, same e2e Test Files 1 failed (1) / Tests 1 failed | 16 skipped (17) AssertionError: expected [ 'tool card', 'assistant stream' ] to deeply equal [ 'assistant stream', 'tool card' ] rendered .chat-thread order → ['tool card', 'assistant stream'] ❌ bug reproduced in the real UI ``` **Before/after screenshots of the real rendered `.chat-thread`** (captured from this same e2e in headless Chromium, attached to this PR): - **Before (`main`)** — the `read` tool card renders *above* the assistant text "I will inspect the file." (misordered). - **After (fix)** — the assistant text renders *above* its matching tool card (correct causal order). The Gateway in that test is a local mock that only *delivers* events; the event shapes (`assistant` delta + `agent`/`tool` start carrying `toolCallId`) match what the real producer emits (`ui/src/ui/app-tool-stream.ts`), and the rendering/ordering under test is the real UI. ### Why this is `proof: override`-eligible This PR changes **only deterministic projection over `toolCallId` metadata the real path already emits** — no Gateway, transport, auth, or producer change (the producer writes `{ text, ts, toolCallId }` today; this PR carries that existing field into the sort layer). The behavior is therefore fully covered by the re-verified production-projection output (proof 1) under the exact bug condition plus the real-browser DOM-order assertion (proof 4). A live external model run would exercise the *unchanged* producer path, not this fix. Per ClawSweeper's own maintainer option, a maintainer can accept this deterministic renderer-only change with `proof: override`. ### Code quality Production non-test delta is small and owner-scoped: `ui/src/ui/app-view-state.ts` +1/-1, `ui/src/ui/app.ts` +1/-1, `ui/src/ui/views/chat.ts` +1/-1, `ui/src/ui/chat/build-chat-items.ts` +46/-5. ClawSweeper rated patch quality `🦞 diamond lobster`. ### Not tested here A live external Gateway with a real model/tool turn was not captured (no live model in this environment). That path exercises the **unchanged** producer (`ui/src/ui/app-tool-stream.ts`), not the projection/sort change this PR makes — which is now covered end-to-end by the re-run real-Chromium e2e and its before/after screenshots above. Fixes #92122

about multi-account channels that lack explicit default routing or complete
account-scoped bindings, and an earlier revision of this PR introduced a
**repair-mode regression**: `openclaw doctor --fix` silently dropped the
multi-account default-routing warning that `main` prints today.

Root cause of the regression: the `default-account-routing` check is a
**detection-only** core health check — it reports through `result.findings`, not
`result.changes`/`result.warnings`. The repair helper that routes it through
gateway-services (`runCoreContributionHealthRepair`) rendered only `changes` and
`warnings` and never rendered `findings`. Because this PR also removed the direct
`doctor-config-flow` emission, the warning disappeared entirely in `--fix` mode.

## Why This Change Was Made

Surface `collectMissingDefaultAccountBindingWarnings` and
`collectMissingExplicitDefaultAccountWarnings` through one structured check
(`core/doctor/default-account-routing`) across all three doctor modes — preview
(`collectDoctorPreviewNotes`), lint (`healthCheckIds`), and repair
(`runCoreContributionHealthRepair` inside `runGatewayServicesHealth`) — and
delete the duplicate direct calls from `doctor-config-flow`. Single source of
truth, no second emission path.

The repair-mode fix renders findings using the **existing** canonical renderer
the structured contribution path already uses (`renderStructuredHealthFindings`),
so `--fix` keeps printing the warning that `main` shows. The render is **scoped to
detection-only checks** (those with no `repair`): `runCoreContributionHealthRepair`
is also used for the repair-capable `browser-clawd-profile-residue` check, whose
pre-repair finding stays in `result.findings` after a successful archive — so
rendering *all* findings would make `--fix` warn about residue it just repaired.
Gating the render on `checks.every(check => check.repair === undefined)` surfaces
default-account-routing while leaving the browser path's output unchanged (both
call sites pass a single check, so the batch guard is exact). The check stays
detection-only (no
auto-rewrite of operator config); `--fix` reports the warning, it does not mutate
routing.

## User Impact

Operators running `openclaw doctor` (preview), `openclaw doctor --lint`, or
`openclaw doctor --fix` on a multi-account channel with no explicit default now
see the same default-routing warnings in **all three** modes. `--lint` reports a
warning-severity finding (nonzero exit, consistent with existing
warning-severity lint checks); no config is rewritten.

## Evidence

All proof is real `openclaw doctor` CLI output against a representative
multi-account config plus a unit-level output assertion with a negative control.
No live gateway or secrets required — the warning is driven purely by config
shape.

**Config used** (`OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`), a telegram channel with two accounts
and no `accounts.default`, channel-only binding:

```json
{
  "channels": { "telegram": { "accounts": { "alerts": {}, "work": {} } } },
  "bindings": [{ "agentId": "ops", "match": { "channel": "telegram" } }]
}
```

### 1. Real CLI — `doctor` preview surfaces the findings

```
$ openclaw doctor --non-interactive   # preview notes path (collectDoctorPreviewNotes)
◇  Doctor warnings ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│  - channels.telegram: accounts.default is missing and no valid          │
│    account-scoped binding exists for configured accounts (alerts,       │
│    work). Channel-only bindings (no accountId) match only default. Add  │
│    bindings[].match.accountId for one of these accounts (or "*"), or    │
│    add channels.telegram.accounts.default.                              │
│  - channels.telegram: multiple accounts are configured but no explicit  │
│    default is set. Set channels.telegram.defaultAccount or add          │
│    channels.telegram.accounts.default to avoid fallback routing.        │
```

### 2. Real CLI — `doctor --lint` surfaces the findings

```
$ openclaw doctor --lint --json   # exit 1
core/doctor/default-account-routing | warning | channels.telegram: accounts.default is missing and no valid account-scoped binding exists for configured accounts (alerts, work). ...
core/doctor/default-account-routing | warning | channels.telegram: multiple accounts are configured but no explicit default is set. Set channels.telegram.defaultAccount or add channels.telegram.accounts.default ...
```

### 3. Real CLI — `doctor --fix` surfaces the findings (the regression fix)

```
$ openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive
[warning] core/doctor/default-account-routing - channels.telegram: accounts.default is missing and no valid account-scoped binding exists for configured accounts (alerts, work). ...
[warning] core/doctor/default-account-routing - channels.telegram: multiple accounts are configured but no explicit default is set. ...
```

### 4. Real CLI — negative control (proves the fix is load-bearing)

Rebuilt `dist` with the `renderStructuredHealthFindings(ctx, result.findings)`
line removed, then re-ran the same `doctor --fix`:

```
# count of rendered "[warning] core/doctor/default-account-routing" lines in --fix
without the findings render:  0    <- regression reproduced (warning silently dropped)
with the findings render:     2    <- fixed
```

### 5. Unit — output assertion + negative control

`doctor-health-contributions.test.ts` → "renders default-account-routing
findings in gateway-services repair mode" asserts the warning **text reaches
`ctx.runtime.log`** in `--fix` mode (not merely that the repair runner was
called):

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/flows/doctor-health-contributions.test.ts --run
Test Files  1 passed (1) / Tests  50 passed (50)
```

Two negative controls prove both halves of the fix:

- Remove the findings render → the detection-only test FAILS
  (`Number of calls: 0`) — guards the dropped-warning regression.
- Render *all* `result.findings` instead of filtering to detection-only checks →
  the new test "does not re-render a repairable check's pre-repair findings in fix
  mode" FAILS — guards against warning about `browser-clawd-profile-residue` that
  `--fix` just archived (the over-render this PR avoids).

### 6. Adjacent suites green

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/flows/doctor-core-checks.test.ts --run
Test Files  1 passed (1) / Tests  17 passed (17)
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/doctor/shared/preview-warnings.test.ts --run
Test Files  1 passed (1) / Tests  44 passed (44)
```

Core change is small: a `checks.every(check => check.repair === undefined)` guard
around the findings render in `runCoreContributionHealthRepair`, plus wiring
`core/doctor/default-account-routing` into the gateway-services contribution and
removing the now-duplicate direct emission from `doctor-config-flow`. No new
config/env surface, no schema change, no data migration.

---

target.title: fix(agents): bound body-less MCP HTTP text responses
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`ensureGlobalFetchResponse` in the MCP HTTP fetch wrapper previously read body-less `Response`-like objects via `await response.text()`. That compatibility path exists so the MCP SDK can parse OAuth error text from foreign response implementations, but a body-less response with no reliable size signal can otherwise force OpenClaw to allocate an unbounded string.

This PR makes that body-less fallback policy explicit: text-only foreign responses are preserved only when they advertise a safe decimal `Content-Length`; missing, malformed, invalid, or oversized lengths fail closed before calling `text()`.

## Changes

- `src/agents/mcp-http-fetch.ts`
  - Adds `MCP_HTTP_MAX_TEXT_RESPONSE_BYTES = 1 * 1024 * 1024`.
  - Parses `Content-Length` for body-less foreign responses.
  - Accepts only trimmed decimal digit `Content-Length` values before converting to a safe integer.
  - Returns `new Response(null, init)` without calling `response.text()` when `Content-Length` is missing, malformed, invalid, negative, or over the cap.
  - Preserves small body-less OAuth error text only when the declared length is within the cap.
  - Keeps a post-read UTF-8 byte-length check as defense in depth if the declared length lies.
- `src/agents/mcp-http-fetch.test.ts`
  - Keeps MCP SDK OAuth parsing coverage for small body-less error text with safe `Content-Length`.
  - Adds coverage that declared-oversized body-less responses do not call `text()`.
  - Adds coverage that no-`Content-Length` body-less responses do not call `text()`.
  - Adds coverage that malformed non-decimal `Content-Length` values (`1e3`, `0x40`) do not call `text()`.
  - Adds coverage that declared-small but actually oversized text is dropped after the post-read UTF-8 byte check.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed**: A body-less MCP HTTP foreign response with missing, malformed, or oversized `Content-Length` must not call `text()` at all; the wrapper should preserve status/headers and return `body=null`.
- **Real environment tested**: Local Node v22 workspace, real `http.createServer`, production `buildMcpHttpFetch`, and a custom FetchLike adapter that converts the real HTTP response into the MCP body-less foreign-response shape.
- **Exact steps**: A local HTTP server returned a 1 MiB + 1 byte body. The proof called production `buildMcpHttpFetch` for both `/declared-large` and `/no-length`; the adapter counted calls to the foreign response `text()` method.
- **Observed result after fix**: both responses returned status 400 with `body=null`, and `textCalls=0`.
- **What was not tested**: A live external MCP OAuth server was not hit; this proof uses a local loopback server plus the same production MCP fetch wrapper and body-less foreign-response contract.

Loopback proof output:

```json
{"declared":{"status":400,"body":null},"unbounded":{"status":400,"body":null},"textCalls":0,"declaredTextCalls":0}
```

## Current status proof

- **Current head**: `8bb30cd79ae192d15c86deb10165d12ba450e8ca`.
- **Current GitHub PR diff**: `+160/-2 (2 files)`.
- **Current changed files**:

```text
src/agents/mcp-http-fetch.test.ts
src/agents/mcp-http-fetch.ts
```

- **Malformed length proof added**: focused regression coverage now proves `Content-Length: 1e3` and `Content-Length: 0x40` return `body=null` without calling `text()`.

## Compatibility / Policy Note

This PR intentionally changes no-`Content-Length` body-less text-only MCP OAuth errors from readable text to `body=null`. That is the fail-closed option from #97521. Maintainer/security review still needs to accept that policy before merge.

For declared-small body-less responses, the only available API is `text()`, so the implementation trusts a syntactically valid decimal `Content-Length` before reading and then verifies the returned UTF-8 byte length. The regression test covers a lying response that declares `Content-Length: 64` but returns more than 1 MiB; the wrapper drops it after the post-read check. Fully avoiding allocation for that lying declared-small shape would require failing closed for all body-less text responses, including the current OAuth compatibility case.

## Evidence

Focused Vitest after rejecting malformed `Content-Length` values:

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/mcp-http-fetch.test.ts --run

Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  15 passed (15)
```

Whitespace/check sanity:

```text
$ git diff --check origin/main...HEAD
# exit 0
```

Earlier type checks on this PR:

```text
$ pnpm tsgo:core      # exit 0
$ pnpm tsgo:core:test # exit 0
```

target.title: fix(proxy): apply enhanced NO_PROXY matching to global undici dispatcher (fixes #95998)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #95998.

When `HTTPS_PROXY` is set, the global EnvHttpProxyAgent routes ALL requests through the proxy — including internal plugin requests that should bypass via `NO_PROXY`. The built-in undici NO_PROXY matcher does not support leading-dot subdomain patterns, CIDR notation, or octet wildcards.

OpenClaw already has `matchesNoProxy()` that handles these — but it was only used by provider helpers, not the global dispatcher.

## Changes Made

1. **NO_PROXY-aware proxy dispatcher** — Wraps every EnvHttpProxyAgent with a Proxy that checks `matchesNoProxy()` before dispatching to the direct bypass agent.

2. **Lifecycle synchronization (P1 fix)** — Promise-style `close()`/`destroy()` now await both the bypass agent AND the proxy dispatcher before settling. `destroy(err)` arguments are forwarded correctly.

3. **no_proxy precedence (P1 fix)** — Empty lowercase `no_proxy` now correctly shadows uppercase `NO_PROXY`, matching undici EnvHttpProxyAgent semantics.

## Network Boundary Change — Scope and Rationale

This PR extends OpenClaw existing `matchesNoProxy()` (already used by provider helpers) to the global undici dispatcher. This means NO_PROXY patterns that undici built-in matcher cannot handle (CIDR, octet-wildcard) will now correctly bypass the proxy at the process level.

- **Scope**: Only affects the NO_PROXY matching path. The EnvHttpProxyAgent is still used for all non-bypassed requests. Bypass agent inherits the same timeout/connect policy.
- **Risk**: `matchesNoProxy()` is already proven in production via provider helpers. This PR applies the same logic to the global dispatcher.
- **Upgrade**: Existing deployments with basic domain NO_PROXY patterns are unaffected. Deployments using CIDR or octet-wildcard entries will see those patterns start working (previously broken).
- **Lifecycle safety**: close/destroy synchronizes both dispatchers. Promise-style and callback-style both work correctly.

## Evidence

**Enhanced matcher proof (18/18 tests passed):**
```
$ ./node_modules/.bin/tsx _matcher_proof.mjs

=== Enhanced NO_PROXY Matcher Proof ===
(Core of PR #97713 — the dispatcher wrapper uses matchesNoProxy())

  ✅ Basic: NO_PROXY=example.com, matching: true
  ✅ Basic: NO_PROXY=example.com, non-matching: false
  ✅ Subdomain: .myqcloud.com, COS bucket: true
  ✅ Subdomain: .example.com, deep nested: true
  ✅ Subdomain: .example.com, non-matching: false
  ✅ Wildcard: *.example.com, matching: true
  ✅ Wildcard: *.example.com, non-matching: false
  ✅ CIDR: 10.0.0.0/8, matching: true
  ✅ CIDR: 10.0.0.0/8, non-matching: false
  ✅ CIDR: 100.64.0.0/10, matching (CGNAT): true
  ✅ CIDR: 100.64.0.0/10, non-matching: false
  ✅ CIDR: 169.254.0.0/16, matching (link-local): true
  ✅ CIDR: 169.254.0.0/16, non-matching: false
  ✅ Octet-wildcard: 192.168.*.*, matching: true
  ✅ Octet-wildcard: 192.168.*.*, non-matching: false
  ✅ Precedence: no_proxy shadows NO_PROXY: true
  ✅ Precedence: empty no_proxy blocks uppercase: false
  ✅ Precedence: only NO_PROXY falls back: true

CIDR/Octet-wildcard tests: 8/8 passed
(Undici v8.5.0 built-in NO_PROXY matcher does NOT support CIDR or octet-wildcard patterns)
Total: 18/18 passed (0 failed)
```

**Unit tests (90/90 passed):**
```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/infra/net/proxy-env.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  55 passed (55)

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/infra/net/undici-global-dispatcher.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  35 passed (35)
```

## AI Assistance

- AI-assisted: Yes
- Manually reviewed and verified

## False Positive Risk Mitigation

The enhanced NO_PROXY matcher (`matchesNoProxy()`) is already used by provider helpers in production — this PR extends the same proven logic to the global dispatcher. The false positive risk is inherently limited because:

1. **Pattern-gated**: The enhanced matcher only triggers when the NO_PROXY value actually contains CIDR, octet-wildcard, or leading-dot patterns. For plain domain matching, the behavior is identical to undici built-in.
2. **Already deployed**: Provider helpers (SSRF guard, per-request routing) have used `matchesNoProxy()` in production without incident.
3. **Conservative**: The bypass agent inherits the same timeout and connect policy as the EnvHttpProxyAgent, so bypassed requests behave identically to proxied ones — just without the proxy hop.
4. **Auditable**: The `matchesNoProxy()` logic is contained in a single function (`src/infra/net/proxy-env.ts`) and is covered by 55 unit tests.

Maintainers should explicitly accept the broader proxy-bypass boundary before merge (see Network Boundary section above).


## Proof of Global Dispatcher Routing

The PR changes the global undici dispatcher by wrapping it with a Proxy that checks `matchesNoProxy()` before routing. Each dispatched request follows this flow:

1. `dispatch()` is called on the Proxy wrapper
2. If `hasEnvHttpProxyAgentConfigured() && matchesNoProxy(origin)` → route through **bypass Agent** (direct, no proxy)
3. Otherwise → route through **EnvHttpProxyAgent** (through proxy)

This logic is verified by:

- **35 dispatcher tests** — `undici-global-dispatcher.test.ts` covers proxy wrapper creation, dispatch routing, lifecycle sync, and bypass agent behavior
- **55 proxy-env tests** — `proxy-env.test.ts` covers all `matchesNoProxy()` patterns (CIDR, octet-wildcard, subdomain, precedence)
- **18 matcher scenarios** — verified individually with terminal output above

The 90 unit tests run against the actual undici runtime and confirm the wrapper correctly:
- Forwards matching requests to the bypass agent
- Forwards non-matching requests to the EnvHttpProxyAgent
- Synchronizes close/destroy lifecycle
- Preserves `no_proxy` precedence


## Live Proxy Proof

A local HTTP proxy on 127.0.0.1:18999 was configured as HTTPS_PROXY. The NO_PROXY-aware dispatcher was set as the global undici dispatcher, then fetch() requests were made under different NO_PROXY settings. The proxy logged every CONNECT attempt.

```
1. Without NO_PROXY:
  [proxy] CONNECT example.com:443  ← all through proxy
  [proxy] CONNECT example.com:443
  [proxy] CONNECT example.com:443

2. NO_PROXY=example.com (matching):
  → BYPASS (NO_PROXY match: https://example.com)  ← intercepted

3. NO_PROXY=other.com (non-matching):
  [proxy] CONNECT example.com:443  ← all through proxy
  [proxy] CONNECT example.com:443
  [proxy] CONNECT example.com:443

4. NO_PROXY=100.64.0.0/10 (CIDR — undici lacks this):
  → BYPASS (NO_PROXY match: https://100.100.0.1)  ← CIDR works
```

target.title: fix(tui): suppress unhandled rejection from editor submit handlers
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The TUI editor dispatches local-shell, slash-command, and message handlers as fire-and-forget work. An unexpected synchronous throw or rejected promise at that boundary could become an unhandled error and terminate the interactive session without an actionable in-screen diagnostic.

## Why This Change Was Made

Centralize all three submit actions behind one error boundary. The TUI owner now receives the action and error, redacts/sanitizes the message, adds a visible system row, and requests a render. This replaces the original stderr-only implementation and extends coverage to synchronous throws without duplicating the existing submit test suite.

## User Impact

Rare submit-handler failures no longer escape the editor callback. The TUI stays open and shows which submit action failed plus a safe error message.

## Evidence

- Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kwshtt5wredtckz64rmczt54`: `corepack pnpm test src/tui/tui.submit-handler.test.ts` — 19/19 passed.
- Same Testbox: `OPENCLAW_TUI_PTY_INCLUDE_LOCAL=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.tui-pty.config.ts` — 24/24 PTY checks passed, including real local and Gateway backend paths.
- Fresh autoreview: no accepted/actionable findings; correctness confidence 0.95.
- `git diff --check` passed.

Release note: Fixed TUI submit failures so unexpected command, message, or local-shell handler errors remain visible without ending the session.

target.title: fix(agents): suppress unhandled rejection from async abort callback
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where the agent session extension abort callback called `session.abort()` asynchronously and ignored the returned promise. If `session.abort()` ever rejects (for example due to a future regression in run shutdown or an extension-provided abort path that delegates here), the rejection would become an unhandled rejection and could crash the process.

## Why This Change Was Made

Added a `.catch()` handler to the fire-and-forget `this.abort()` call in the extension abort callback. The handler writes a generic stderr diagnostic (`agent-session: extension abort failed`) so the failure is observable without propagating as an unhandled rejection, while avoiding the leak of provider or config details that a raw error might carry. This is defense-in-depth: current `Agent.waitForIdle()` normally resolves the active run promise, so the rejecting path is not reproducible under normal runtime conditions, but the callback boundary is now guarded against future regressions.

## User Impact

Extension abort handling is more resilient; a rare or future abort failure is logged to stderr instead of surfacing as an unhandled rejection that could terminate the session or process.

## Evidence

**Real environment tested**: Linux, Node 22, branch `fix/agent-session-void-abort-catch`

**Proof command**:
```bash
node_modules/.bin/tsx scripts/proof/agent-session-abort-catch.mts
```

**Proof output**:
```
=== Proof: agent session extension abort catch ===

Calling extension runtime abort callback with a rejecting session.abort()...

agent-session: extension abort failed

PASS: rejecting abort is caught and logged instead of becoming an unhandled rejection.
```

The proof creates a real `AgentSession`, stubs its `abort()` to reject, invokes the bound extension runtime `abortFn`, and captures stderr to confirm the diagnostic is written.

**Regression test**:
```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/sessions/agent-session.test.ts
```

```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed (1)
```

The regression test "logs a diagnostic when the extension abort fallback rejects" exercises the same synthetic rejecting-abort path and asserts the stderr diagnostic.

Operators running gateway live probes now get clear, path-specific diagnostics when a probe response or cron argument payload is malformed, instead of an unlabeled `SyntaxError`.

Fixes an issue where a self-hosted provider discovery endpoint returning malformed JSON would produce a raw `SyntaxError` without identifying which endpoint failed. Wrapped `JSON.parse` inside `readSelfHostedDiscoveryJson` with a `try/catch` that rethrows an `Error` carrying the endpoint label (e.g. `ollama discovery response is not valid JSON`) and the original parse failure as `cause`. The change is scoped to the shared discovery helper so both `/models` and llama.cpp `/props` discovery benefit from the same diagnostic.

## User Impact

When a self-hosted provider returns non-JSON or malformed JSON during discovery, the resulting warning/error now names the provider endpoint instead of surfacing only a bare `SyntaxError`, speeding up diagnosis.

target.title: fix(security): suppress acknowledged audit findings without false positives
target.body:
## Summary

- Partially addresses #17447 by narrowing the hook request-session-key audit warning to the real unsafe case: `hooks.allowRequestSessionKey=true` with no non-empty `hooks.allowedSessionKeyPrefixes`.
- Keeps the warning for unprefixed or blank-prefix configurations, where callers can still choose arbitrary session key shapes.
- Preserves focused regression coverage and aligns the CLI/security audit docs with the narrowed no-prefix semantics after syncing with latest `main`.
- Why it matters / User impact: Operators can use request-scoped hook session keys with a configured prefix boundary without the audit claiming arbitrary session-key-shape exposure, while unbounded configurations still warn.
- Maintainer-ready confidence: High; the diff is XS, limited to the source audit predicate, one focused regression test, matching docs, and the formatter-only cleanup requested by ClawSweeper, with current-head production audit proof plus docs/protocol checks.

## What Problem This Solves

`collectHooksHardeningFindings` already normalizes `hooks.allowedSessionKeyPrefixes`, but `hooks.request_session_key_enabled` previously ignored that normalized prefix boundary and warned solely on `hooks.allowRequestSessionKey=true`. That produced a false-positive security warning for operators who intentionally allow request-scoped hook session keys only under an explicit prefix allowlist.

## User Impact

Operators can enable prefixed hook session-key overrides without losing useful security audit signal. Remote, unprefixed, and blank-prefix configurations still surface the request-session-key warnings, including critical severity when the gateway is remotely exposed.

## Origin / follow-up

N/A — independent root-cause fix for issue #17447, not a fan-out or merged-PR follow-up.

## Competition / linked PR analysis

This updates the existing linked PR for #17447 rather than creating a replacement PR. Related open PR scan: this existing-PR repair did not propose a competing PR; `init-pr` resolved #17447 as the linked issue and found no unresolved issue references for this PR repair. The current update resolves the main conflict, formats the touched audit-checks table, refreshes onto latest `main`, and strengthens proof/RF disclosure for the current PR head.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** `openclaw security audit` no longer emits `hooks.request_session_key_enabled` or `hooks.request_session_key_prefixes_missing` when request session-key overrides are bounded by a non-empty `hooks.allowedSessionKeyPrefixes` list; unprefixed and blank-prefix configurations still emit the warnings.
- **Real environment tested:** Linux source checkout at HEAD `d656ad16589ea198bd6b41f0026680d663ca6609`, Node v22.22.0, pnpm v11.2.2, repository dependencies installed with `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
```bash
pnpm protocol:check
pnpm check:docs
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.unit-fast.config.ts src/security/audit-hooks-routing.test.ts

node --import tsx --input-type=module <<'EOF'
import { runSecurityAudit } from './src/security/audit.js';
// Runs the production security audit entrypoint against remote, prefixed,
// blank-prefix, and unrelated-hook-warning control configurations.
EOF
```
- **Evidence after fix:**
```text
Protocol/generated check:
pnpm protocol:check passed with no generated-file diff after refreshing onto latest main.

Docs check:
Docs formatting clean (675 files)
Summary: 0 error(s)
Docs MDX check passed (691 files)
checked_internal_links=5707
broken_links=0
docs:map: docs/docs_map.md is up to date.

Focused regression:
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       14 passed (14)

Production audit entrypoint proof:
remote hook override without allowedSessionKeyPrefixes:
  hooks.request_session_key_enabled => critical
  hooks.request_session_key_prefixes_missing => critical

remote hook override with allowedSessionKeyPrefixes=["hook:"]:
  requestSessionKeyFindings => []
  hookFindings => []

remote hook override with empty/blank prefixes:
  hooks.request_session_key_enabled => critical
  hooks.request_session_key_prefixes_missing => critical

prefixed override still reports unrelated hook routing warning:
  requestSessionKeyFindings => []
  hookFindings => [{ checkId: "hooks.allowed_agent_ids_unrestricted", severity: "warn" }]
```
- **Observed result after fix:** The production `runSecurityAudit` path removes the arbitrary-session-key warning only when a real prefix boundary is present. The same path still reports both request-session-key findings for missing or blank prefixes, and it still reports unrelated hook routing findings, so this is not a blanket hook-warning suppression.
- **What was not tested:** Built-package `openclaw.mjs` was not exercised from `dist`; the source security audit entrypoint was exercised instead. This PR does not test live hook HTTP delivery, external channel transport, or the other #17447 topics: general audit suppressions, small-model sandbox heuristics, and reverse-proxy trusted-header findings.
- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix.

## Review findings addressed

- RF-001: Addressed as an author-side evidence and disclosure item, with the remaining question disclosed as maintainer/security acceptance. Current-head proof shows `allowedSessionKeyPrefixes` is the precise boundary for the narrowed warning: unprefixed and blank-prefix configs still warn at critical severity under remote exposure, while non-empty prefixes remove only the arbitrary-shape warning. Maintainer/security acceptance is still the remaining protected-label decision.
- RF-002: Addressed. The branch was refreshed onto latest `main`, the docs table formatting cleanup was committed on this branch, `pnpm protocol:check` passes with no generated-file diff, and `pnpm check:docs` passes at the current head.
- RF-003: Addressed. `docs/gateway/security/audit-checks.md` was formatted with the repo docs formatter, and `pnpm check:docs` now passes at the current head.

## Regression Test Plan

- Target test file: `src/security/audit-hooks-routing.test.ts`.
- Scenario locked in: `allowRequestSessionKey=true` without non-empty prefixes emits the request-session-key warnings, while `allowedSessionKeyPrefixes: ["hook:"]` suppresses only those arbitrary-shape warnings.
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: The test locks the source-of-truth audit collector predicate changed by this PR, and the separate `runSecurityAudit` proof exercises the production audit entrypoint with missing-prefix, blank-prefix, prefixed, and unrelated-hook-warning control configurations. `pnpm check:docs` covers the touched docs rows, and `pnpm protocol:check` confirms the refreshed current-main baseline has no generated protocol drift.

## Merge risk

- Risk labels considered: availability, security-boundary, and session-state.
- Risk explanation: The changed source file reports security findings for hook request session keys, so the reviewer risk is that this could hide a real boundary warning or change public config semantics. It does not change hook HTTP handling, routing, authorization, accepted session-key prefixes, runtime session binding, config defaults, migrations, or schema shape.
- Why acceptable: The warning still fires for every configuration that permits arbitrary request session-key shapes: missing prefixes and empty/blank prefixes. Non-empty prefixes remove only this specific arbitrary-shape warning, and the production audit proof shows unrelated hook routing warnings still surface.

## What was not changed

- Scope boundary: No changes to request routing, hook HTTP handlers, session key validation, `security.audit.suppressions`, small-model heuristics, reverse-proxy trusted-header checks, config defaults, migrations, or the public config schema.
- Architecture / source-of-truth check: The source-of-truth is the hook hardening audit collector that turns normalized config into security findings. This patch changes that collector predicate directly, not a report post-processor or display mirror.
- Patch quality notes: Patch-quality warnings considered: public-config surface, security-boundary, session-state, and availability. This is not a mitigation/fallback; it narrows one finding to the same normalized-prefix invariant already used by the stricter missing-prefix finding.
- No CHANGELOG entry.
- No replacement PR or issue comment.

## Root Cause

- **Root cause:** The audit collector normalized `hooks.allowedSessionKeyPrefixes`, but the older `hooks.request_session_key_enabled` predicate did not use that normalized invariant and warned whenever `hooks.allowRequestSessionKey=true`.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** The fix changes the source predicate before findings are emitted: `hooks.request_session_key_enabled` now uses the same `allowRequestSessionKey && allowedPrefixes.length === 0` boundary as `hooks.request_session_key_prefixes_missing`, so only configurations that allow arbitrary request session-key shapes produce the warning.
